name: Manuel Martínez Bautista
summary: Manuel Martínez Bautista, a Nahuatl Indigenous farmer from the community of Crisolco in Yahualica, Hidalgo, was found dead on 24 December 2018 after being attacked with a machete. Bautista was a land defender.

name: Sinar Corzo Esquinca
summary: Sinar Corzo Esquinca was assassinated on 3 January 2019 in Chiapas. He was a member of the Comité Ciudadano de Defensa de los Derechos Humanos Coloso de Piedra and, like many defenders, had received threats before he was killed.

name: Gustavo Cruz Mendoza
summary: Gustavo Cruz Mendoza was killed in Santiago Jocotepec, Oaxaca after being abducted from his home by unknown men. He was a Chinantec man, a land defender, and member of the Popular Indigenous Council of Oaxaca “Ricardo Flores Magón” (CIPO-RFM).

name: Bernardino García Hernández
summary: Bernardino García Hernández, an activist and Indigenous Mixtec land defender, was found killed from gunshots on 21 January 2019. He was a peace mediator, and in 2010 represented Zimatlán de Lázaro Cárdenas before the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights seeking a negotiated settlement of his community's conflict with San Sebastián Nopalera in the Mixtec region.

name: José Santiago Álvarez Gómez
summary: José Santiago Álvarez Gómez, a Tsotsil man and activist, was kidnapped, tortured and murdered in Amatán, Chiapas, alongside Noé Jiménez Pablo on 28 January 2019. He was a member of the Movement for Well-being, Peace and the Common Good of Amatán. He was enrolled in the Protection Mechanism for Human Rights Defenders and Journalists.

name: Noé Jiménez Pablo
summary: Noé Jiménez Pablo, a Tsotsil man and activist, was kidnapped, tortured and murdered in Amatán, Chiapas, alongside José Santiago Álvarez Gómez on 28 January 2019. He belonged to the National Coordinating Committee Plan de Ayala–National Movement (CNPA-MN) and to the Movement for Well-being, Peace and the Common Good of Amatán. He was enrolled in the Protection Mechanism for Human Rights Defenders and Journalists.

name: Estelina López Gómez
summary: Estelina López Gómez was shot in the abdomen and the head by an armed group in the community of Santo Tomás, Amatenango, Chiapas, after she got out of a pickup truck to open a gate. López was a land and territory defender and a member of the organisation Luz y Fuerza del Pueblo, which linked her killing to an attempt to dispossess the group of its land.

name: Oscar Cazorla
summary: Oscar Cazorla, a gay rights activist, was found in his home in Juchitán, Oaxaca on 9 February 2019 with signs of torture on his body.

name: Rubén Fajardo
beat: Member of the National Citizen Council and human rights observer. He worked professionally as a mechanic.
summary: Rubén Fajardo was shot in the head and back by two men on a motorcycle while he was walking in Morelos on 18 February 2019. He was a human rights observer and was in charge of a civil organization in Yautepec, Cuautla, and Jiutepec. Fajardo's last public appearance was at a conference on the viability of the operation of the thermoelectric plant in the town of Huexca, in the municipality of Yecapixtla.

name: Eulodia Lilia Díaz Ortiz
summary: Eulodia Lilia Díaz Ortiz was shot dead at her home in Santiago Tianguistenco, State of Mexico, in front of her son and daughter-in-law. Díaz was a member of the Consejo Indígena de Trueque and had defended the community's Tianguis del Trueque, a barter market run autonomously by Otomí, Tlahuica and Nahua people, against municipal attempts to take it over.

name: Abiram Hernández Fernández
summary: Abiram Hernández Fernández was found dead in his home in the Arboledas del Sumidero neighbourhood of Xalapa, Veracruz on 30 March 2019, having died of severe head trauma. Hernández coordinated the civil organisation Centro de Servicios Municipales Heriberto Jara and belonged to the Colectivo por la Paz Xalapa, accompanying families of disappeared people through legal proceedings.

name: Camilo Álvarez Pérez
summary: Camilo Álvarez Pérez was ambushed and killed in Michoacán. The record gives no further detail on the attack.

name: Luis Armando Fuentes Aquino
summary: Luis Armando Fuentes Aquino, a Zapotec community defender, was shot dead in San Francisco Ixhuatán, Oaxaca. He belonged to the Corriente del Pueblo Sol Rojo and to the Comisión en Defensa de la Tierra y el Territorio de la Zona Oriente del Istmo, campaigned with the Network of Resistance Against High Electricity Rates, and defended the territory of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec.

name: Héctor Mauricio Rosas Hernández
summary: Héctor Mauricio Rosas Hernández, known as “Mub Times”, was murdered in the Obrera neighbourhood of Guanajuato while running a project to draw young people out of the streets. He was a DJ and a member of the Mundo Ritual Association, A.C.

name: Héctor Armando Domínguez
summary: Héctor Armando Domínguez, a muralist and visual artist who championed urban art, was killed in Ciudad Valles, San Luis Potosí. His father, Aureliano Domínguez, and his brother, Julio Emmanuel Domínguez Rodríguez, were killed in the same attack. His works had been vandalised on several occasions.

name: Gregorio Chaparro Cruz
summary: Gregorio Chaparro Cruz, a Rarámuri man and defender of the Coloradas de la Virgen forest, was shot dead outside his home in the municipality of Guadalupe y Calvo, on the Chihuahua–Sinaloa border, together with his mother, Otilia Martínez Cruz. The two had for years defended Rarámuri territory against illegal logging. The killings are attributed to the criminal group Los Chorohuis, an attribution the record marks as unconfirmed.

name: Otilia Martínez Cruz
summary: Otilia Martínez Cruz, a Rarámuri woman and niece of the environmental defender Julián Carrillo, who was killed in 2018, was shot multiple times outside her home in the municipality of Guadalupe y Calvo, on the Chihuahua–Sinaloa border, together with her son Gregorio Chaparro Cruz. The two had for years defended Rarámuri territory against illegal logging; the killings are attributed to the criminal group Los Chorohuis, an attribution the record marks as unconfirmed. At least ten activists and defenders in the Sierra Tarahumara had been killed for defending the forests in the preceding years.

name: Eugenio Máximo Hilario
summary: Eugenio Máximo Hilario was murdered in Hueycantenango, Guerrero. A Nahua leader, he headed the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ) and had been a regional commander of the Regional Coordinator of Community Authorities – Founding Peoples (CRAC-PF).

name: José Lucio Bartolo Faustino
summary: José Lucio Bartolo Faustino, a Nahua man, was murdered in Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero on 4 May 2019, alongside his colleague Modesto Verales Sebastián. He was a councillor on the Indigenous Governing Council, a promoter of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ) and regional coordinator for the CRAC-PF committee.

name: Modesto Verales Sebastián
summary: Modesto Verales Sebastián, a Nahua man and promoter of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ), was assassinated in Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero on 4 May 2019, alongside his colleague José Lucio Bartolo Faustino.

name: Leonel Díaz Urbano
summary: Leonel Díaz Urbano was shot dead at his home in San Juan Tahitic, in the Sierra Norte of Puebla, on the night of 9 May 2019. Díaz was an Indigenous leader who since 2016 had organised residents against the hydroelectric plant the company Hidroeléctrica Gaya sought to build on the Apulco River.

name: Bartolo Morales Hilario
summary: Bartolo Morales Hilario and Isaías Xanteco Ahuejote disappeared near Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero, on 23 May 2019. Their dismembered bodies were found the next morning in black bags on the Chilapa–Tlapa highway. Hilario was a Nahua member of the Regional Coordinator of Community Authorities–Founding Peoples (CRAC-PF) and a promoter of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ), part of the National Indigenous Congress.

name: Isaías Xanteco Ahuejote
summary: Isaías Xanteco Ahuejote and Bartolo Hilario Morales disappeared near Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero, on 23 May 2019. Their dismembered bodies were found the next morning in black bags on the Chilapa–Tlapa highway. Xanteco was a Nahua member of the community police of the Regional Coordinator of Community Authorities – Founding Peoples (CRAC-PF) from Xicotlán and a local promoter of CIPOG-EZ.

name: José Luis Álvarez Flores
outlet: Environmental activist
beat: José Luis Álvarez Flores served as head of the Wildlife Conservation Management Unit known as “UMA Saraguato” in Chiapas. In addition to safeguarding this species that inhabits the jungles of southeastern Mexico, he was dedicated to the care of the beaches and coastal area of ​​the Ejido Calatraba, in Palenque. He was a public advocate against sand extraction, and a defender of the Usumacinta River.
summary: José Luis Álvarez Flores's body was found on 10 June 2019 beside the highway between Chiapas and Tabasco, near the Calatraba ejido, alongside narcomensaje signs carrying threats against his family and allies. Álvarez ran the UMA Saraguato wildlife conservation management unit and worked to protect beaches and coastal areas in Ejido Calatraba, Palenque, Chiapas.

name: Mario Moreno López
summary: Mario Moreno López was murdered in the municipality of Venustiano Carranza, Chiapas on 18 June 2019. He was a member of the National Front for the Struggle for Socialism.

name: Javier Campos Morales
summary: Javier Campos Morales, a Jesuit priest, was shot dead inside a church in Urique, Chihuahua, on 20 June 2022. A second priest and advocate, Joaquín Mora, was murdered with him. Campos was ordained in 1972 and had served Rarámuri communities in the Sierra Tarahumara since 1974, supporting community causes and the defence of territory and natural resources.

name: Maria Cristina Vázquez Chavarría
outlet: Acitvist against real estate developments in Mexico City's Hipódromo-Condesa neighborhood.
summary: María Cristina Vázquez Chavarría was found dead in her flat in the Hipódromo Condesa neighbourhood of Mexico City on 27 June 2019, several days after she was killed. Her body was naked and showed signs of torture. Vázquez was an urban rights activist and a member of her local neighbourhood committee, and alleged threats from property developers were among the lines of investigation.

name: Salvadora Chávez Rendón
summary: Salvadora Chávez Rendón, a Nahua woman, was killed on 11 July 2019 when armed men in civilian clothes intercepted and opened fire on the truck carrying her and ten others on the road from Lamazintla to Cantera Rosa, in Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero. She was returning from Chilapa, where she had pressed a complaint against members of the CRAC-PF community police over the killing of five people in February 2015, among them her husband.

name: Zenaida Pulido Lonbera
summary: Zenaida Pulido Lonbera was shot dead on the coastal highway near Pichilinguillo, Aquila, Michoacán on 19 July 2019. She was searching for her missing husband, Elidio Cisneros, and was allegedly murdered for her activism in the search for victims of enforced disappearance and clandestine graves.

name: Miguel Ángel Medina Lara
beat: Seems more hate crime than activism related
summary: Miguel Ángel Medina Lara was beaten and stoned to death in Acayucan, Veracruz on 22 August 2019. His body was found in the municipal cemetery a day after he failed to return home from a theatre workshop. Medina was an activist and promoter of LGBT+ rights. Relatives and activists said the killing bore the aggravating features of a hate crime based on his sexual orientation.

name: Nora López León
summary: Nora López León was found dead from multiple stab wounds in Chiapas on 21 August 2019. She was an environmental activist in charge of the red macaw breeding project at the Aluxes Ecotourism Park.

name: Isaías Cantú Carrasco
summary: Isaías Cantú Carrasco, a Me'phaa man, was killed with a firearm on 11 October 2019 in Guerrero. He was president of the Comisariado de Bienes Comunales of Paraje Montero, in the municipality of Malinaltepec, and a member of the Consejo Regional de Autoridades Agrarias en Defensa del Territorio; for seven years he had defended communal territory against gold and silver mining.

name: Paul Humberto Vizcarra Ruiz
outlet: Environmental activist from Morelos
summary: Paul Humberto Vizcarra Ruiz went missing on 14 October 2019. His body was found two days later near the Autopista del Sol, close to the village of Parres in Tlalpan, Mexico City, with his wrists bound. Vizcarra was a Morelos businessman and environmental campaigner who promoted waste reduction and recycling.

name: Cruz Soto Caraveo
summary: Cruz Soto Caraveo was illegally detained by several police officers in Guazapares, Chihuahua, and then murdered on 20 October 2019 by order of the director of the Municipal Police. The former policemen were sentenced to 12 years in prison. Soto was a member of the Collective of Families Forcibly Displaced from the Sierra Tarahumara. He had received threats for several years.

name: Arnulfo Cerón Soriano
summary: Arnulfo Cerón Soriano was disappeared on 11 October 2019 and subsequently killed; his death was announced on 20 November 2019. He was a human rights defender in La Montaña de Guerrero and a member of the Frente Popular de la Montaña. He and his organisation had been subjected to constant public discrediting campaigns and harassment by municipal authorities, and the record describes his case as a clear example of stigmatisation preceding violence.

name: Catalino Barradas Santiago
summary: Catalino Barradas Santiago, a Chatino land defender from Santa Lucía Teotepec, was shot dead by municipal police officers of Santos Reyes Nopala, on the Oaxaca coast, at about 9 p.m. on 30 November 2019. He was among residents acting as election watchers who had stopped a vehicle said to be campaigning illegally. On the road home, a police patrol cut them off and officers opened fire.

name: Manuel Alejandro Gutiérrez
beat: Member of the CRAC-PC Regional Council and founder of the Huamuxtitlán Community Police Group Liaison Committee
summary: Manuel Alejandro Gutiérrez was killed in an ambush in Puebla. He was a regional advisor for the CRAC-PC Huamuxtitlán-Olinalá Liaison Committee, and was a member of the Centro Nacional de Comunicación Social AC.

name: Josué Bernardo Marcial Santos
summary: Josué Bernardo Marcial Santos was murdered in Veracruz and found in the trunk of a car on Federal Highway 145, between Sayula and Ciudad Alemánon on 16 December 2019. He was a founding member and active participant in the Altepee collective, and

name: Isabel Cabanillas de la Torre
summary: Isabel Cabanillas de la Torre was shot and killed while riding her bicycle home in downtown Ciudad Juárez. She sought to draw attention to the gender-based violence, and advocated for women's rights. Cabanillas volunteered for the Mesa de Mujeres network's Citizen Gender Observatory project legal impunity in cases of violence against women, and was a member of Hijas De Su Maquilera Madre.

name: Homero Gómez González
summary: Homero Gómez González disappeared on 13 January 2020 and was found dead in a well, his body bearing signs of torture, on 30 January near Ocampo, Michoacán. Gómez managed and defended the El Rosario monarch butterfly sanctuary. The state human rights commission said his forest-protection work was likely affecting the interests of illegal loggers.

name: Raúl Hernández Romero
summary: Raúl Hernández Romero went missing on 27 January 2020. His body was found five days later between Ocampo and Angangueo, Michoacán. Hernández was a nature defender and a tour guide at the El Rosario monarch butterfly sanctuary in Ocampo.

name: Paulina Gómez Palacio Escudero
summary: Paulina Gómez Palacio Escudero went missing on 19 March 2020. Her body was found three days later with gunshot wounds in the municipality of El Salvador, Zacatecas. Escudero was a small-scale farmer and a guardian of the sacred Wixárika territory of Wirikuta, and a long-standing opponent of mining there.

name: Isaac Medardo Herrera Avilés
summary: Isaac Medardo Herrera Avilés was shot at point-blank range when he opened the door of his home in Jiutepec, Morelos, on the night of 23 March 2020. As a lawyer, he spent four years defending the Los Venados nature reserve against a proposed housing development and was the legal representative of the 13 villages defending the Chihuahuita water spring.

name: Karla Valentina Camarena del Castillo
summary: Karla Valentina Camarena del Castillo was shot and killed in San Felipe, Guanajuato on 29 March 2020. She was a transgender rights activists and served as Guanajuato's state coordinator of the Mexican Network of Trans Women.

name: Benito Peralta Arias
summary: Benito Peralta Arias, a Nahua leader of San Jerónimo Amanalco in Texcoco, State of Mexico, was abducted and forced into a vehicle on 21 February 2020. Several days later, a video was released by an armed group alleging they had killed him. Weeks before his disappearance, Peralta had led a movement against insecurity and alleged fuel theft in San Jeronimo that involved police collusion.

name: Adán Vez Lira
summary: Adán Vez Lira was attacked and shot dead on 8 April 2020 while riding a motorcycle near his community in Actopan, Veracruz. For more than two decades he had defended the territory and the birdwatching sanctuary at La Mancha, working to protect mangroves, dunes, and coastal ecosystems. In his final years took part in the resistance to open-pit mining.

name: Esteban Martínez Pérez
summary: Esteban Martínez Pérez was murdered in Putla de Guerrero, Oaxaca, alongside Pablo Guzmán Solano. He was an activist with the Triqui Unified Struggle Movement (MULT).

name: Pablo Guzmán Solano
summary: Pablo Guzmán Solano was shot dead in Putla de Guerrero, Oaxaca, alongside Esteban Martínez Pérez. He was an activist with the Triqui Unified Struggle Movement (MULT).

name: Juan Zamarripa Torres
summary: Juan Zamarripa Torres was murdered at his home in San Juanito, in the municipality of Bocoyna, Chihuahua, together with two family members on 11 April 2020. One line of investigation held that his killing was linked to the effect of his environmental work on criminal groups engaged in illegal logging in the Rarámuri region.

name: Eugui Roy Martínez Pérez
summary: Eugui Roy Martínez Pérez was shot dead at his family's ranch in the community of Tierra Blanca, San Agustín Loxicha, Oaxaca on 7 May 2020. A biology student at the Instituto Tecnológico del Valle de Oaxaca, he had worked since age 11 to rescue and protect reptiles, amphibians and other wild species.

name: Óscar Ontiveros Martínez
summary: Óscar Ontiveros Martínez was killed in Cocula, Guerrero on 12 May 2020. Martínez was a mining leader who fought for labor rights at the Media Luna mine. He was a key figure in the strike that ended in 2018.

name: Umber Gómez González
summary: Umber Gómez González disappeared on 28 May 2020 and was found dead on 1 June 2020 in Siltepec, Chiapas. He was an activist with the Emiliano Zapata Proletarian Organization – Social Organizations Front of Chiapas.

name: José Antonio Montes Enríquez
summary: José Antonio Montes Enríquez was killed and his body found in Bocoyna, Chihuahua. on 6 June 2020. A Rarámuri leader of the Bosques de San Elías Repechique community, he opposed illegal logging and the expansion of the regional airport. Enríquez had survived earlier armed attacks and his house had been set on fire earlier that year.

name: Dr. María Elizabeth Montaño Fernández
summary: Dr. María Elizabeth Montaño Fernández was murdered in Mexico City on 19 June 2020. Dr. Fernandez was had been missing for ten days and her body was found. She was a transgender rights activist, doctor, and medical educator.

name: Jesús Miguel Jerónimo
summary: Jesús Miguel Jerónimo was shot dead at about 11 p.m. on 23 July 2020 at his home in Chilchota, Michoacán, together with his 18-year-old son Jesús Miguel Junior. He was the Jefe de Tenencia (head of land tenure) of the Purépecha community of Ichán, part of the Consejo Supremo Indígena de Michoacán.

name: Jonathan Santos
summary: Jonathan Santos was killed by a gunshot to the head in Zapopan, Jalisco on 11 August 2020. He was an activist and defender of LGBTQ+ rights.

name: Javier Eduardo Pérez Hidalgo
summary: Javier Eduardo Pérez Hidalgo was murdered in Acapancingo, Morelos on 19 August 2020. His body was found burned with signs of torture, and wrapped in a rainbow flag. A hate message was found next to his body. Hidalgo was an activist and defender of LGBTQ+ rights.

name: Tomás Martínez Pinacho
summary: Tomás Martínez Pinacho was shot dead by unidentified gunmen in Ánimas Trujano, Oaxaca on 24 August 2020. He was on his way home from a protest in Oaxaca, at which he had demanded justice for murdered colleagues. He led the Popular Revolutionary Front (FPR) in the Sierra Sur and was a territory defender.

name: Jeanine Huerta López
summary: Jeanine Huerta López was found stabbed to death in Tijuana, Baja California on 27 August 2020. She was an activist who defended the rights of the LGBTQ+ community and of people living with HIV.

name: Mireya Rodríguez Lemus
summary: Mireya Rodríguez Lemus was stabbed 24 times in Aquiles Serdán, Chihuahua on 2 September 2020. She was the founder and president of the organization Unión y Fuerza de Mujeres Trans Chihuahuenses, and promoted LGBTQ+ rights.

name: Óscar Eyraud Adams
summary: Óscar Eyraud Adams was shot dead in Tecate, Baja California on 24 September 2020. A Kumiai water defender from the Juntas de Nejí community, he had publicly denounced the diversion and hoarding of the community's water by companies in Tecate, including the refusal of the national water commission to grant his community a well while granting wells to a local brewery.

name: Daniel Sotelo
summary: Daniel Sotelo was shot dead inside a grocery store owned by his family in Tecate, Baja California on 25 September 2020, the day after his brother-in-law Óscar Eyraud Adams was killed. Sotelo was Kumiai and, like Eyraud, had campaigned against the diversion of local water supplies by large corporations.

name: María del Rosario Zavala Aguilar
summary: María del Rosario Zavala Aguilar was shot dead in her own home in Guanajuato by two assailants on 14 October 2020. She was an advocate for families with missing loved ones, after her son was forcibly disappeared.

name: Juan Aquino González
summary: Juan Aquino González was shot dead in Copalillo, Guerrero on 28 October 2020. A Nahua environmental defender, he founded the Cerro de Tecaballo ecological reserve for macaws and bats, and a game reserve protecting wild boar and hares.

name: Rodolfo Díaz Jiménez
summary: Rodolfo Díaz Jiménez was shot dead by armed men who opened fire while on the car he was driving. Two other men accompanying Jiménez were disappeared. He was a Zapotec social activist in the community assembly of San Baltazar Loxicha, Oaxaca.

name: Gabino Ávila Martínez
summary: Gabino Ávila Martínez was shot dead in Santiago Juxtlahuaca, Oaxaca on 20 November 2020. He was a Triqui leader of the Triqui Unification and Struggle Movement (MULT), and was coordinator of the MULT's political committee. Martínez had received death threats since March 2019.

name: Maurilio Hernández Martínez
summary: Maurilio Hernández Martínez was shot and killed by two men on motorcycles in Santiago Juxtlahuaca, Oaxaca on 25 November 2020. He was a Triqui community police officer from the community of Río Metate, and a member of the Triqui Unification and Struggle Movement (MULT).

name: María Eufemia Reyes Esquivel
summary: María Eufemia Reyes Esquivel was killed in Zitácuaro, Michoacán, alongside Manuel Carmona Esquivel and José Luis Chávez. A Purépecha man, he was a defender of Indigenous autonomy.

name: Amalia Morales Guapango
summary: Amalia Morales Guapango was found tortured and murdered on the Chilapa–Tlapa highway in Guerrero on 20 December 2020 together with three fellow members of her organisation; the four were bound and shot at close range. She was a Nahua member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ), which campaigns for territorial rights, autonomy and self-determination.

name: José Benito Migueleño
summary: José Benito Migueleño was found tortured and murdered on the Chilapa–Tlapa highway in Guerrero on 20 December 2020 together with three fellow members of his organisation; the four were bound and shot at close range. He was a Nahua member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ), which campaigns for territorial rights, autonomy and self-determination.

name: María Agustín Chino
summary: María Agustín Chino was found tortured and murdered on the Chilapa–Tlapa highway in Guerrero on 20 December 2020 together with three fellow members of her organisation; the four were bound and shot at close range. She was a Nahua member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ), which campaigns for territorial rights, autonomy and self-determination.

name: Miguel Migueleño
summary: Miguel Migueleño was found tortured and murdered on the Chilapa–Tlapa highway in Guerrero on 20 December 2020 together with three fellow members of his organisation; the four were bound and shot at close range. He was a Nahua member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ), which campaigns for territorial rights, autonomy and self-determination.

name: Teódulo Gorostieta
summary: Teódulo Gorostieta Domínguez, was one of twelve people killed in a single attack at the Ejido Alto Uxpanapa, Las Choapas, Veracruz, on 17 January 2021. The victims were found with their faces bound with insulating tape, tied hand and foot, and each shot at least once in the head. He had led the self-defense group of Cerro de Nanchital since July 2020.

name: Fidel Heras Cruz
summary: Fidel Heras Cruz was shot by unidentified assailants in his car in La Esperanza, in Santiago Jamiltepec, Oaxaca on 23 January 2021. He chaired the Paso de la Reina ejido and was an active member of the Council of United Peoples for the Defense of the Verde River, opposing the construction of a hydroelectric station on the Río Verde. He had received death threats and had spotted a suspicious vehicle near his home two days before he was killed.

name: Miguel Vázquez Martínez
summary: Miguel Vázquez Martínez was kidnapped on 20 November 2020 and held for ransom; his body was found more than 100 days later on 13 February 2021 at a clandestine burial site in Tlapacoyan, Veracruz. He was a defender of water and guardian of the Bobos River, and founded the Alliance of Communities and Organizations for the Defense of the Bobos-Nautla River and Tecolutla in opposition to hydroelectric, mining and fracking projects.

name: Ramiro Rodríguez Santiz
summary: Ramiro Rodríguez Sántiz was shot in the back on 20 February 2021 as he walked to his milpa in the municipality of Ocosingo, Chiapas in an extrajudicial killing attributed to the paramilitary group Los Petules. He was a member of the Frente Nacional de Lucha por el Socialismo and had been detained and tortured by the same group in 2014 and repeatedly threatened.

name: Noé Robles Cruz
summary: Noé Robles Cruz was shot dead in Barrio Chico, Paso de la Reina, Oaxaca on 14 March 2021 while on duty as an alternate community police officer. He was killed alongside Raymundo Robles Riaño and Gerardo Mendoza Reyes, and the assailants were never identified. He was a community member and defender of the Río Verde.

name: Gerardo Mendoza Reyes
summary: Gerardo Mendoza Reyes was shot dead in Barrio Chico, Paso de la Reina, Oaxaca on 14 March 2021 while on duty as an alternate community police officer. He was killed alongside Raymundo Robles Riaño and Noé Robles Cruz, and the assailants were never identified. He was a defender of the river and of the natural environment around it.

name: Isaias Elacio Palma
summary: Isaías Elacio Palma was killed in a direct shooting in Cacahuatepec, Guerrero. He was a founding member of the Council of Ejidos and Communities Opposed to the La Parota Dam (CECOP) and of the CRAC-PC community police force and defended the Papagayo River against the La Parota dam. His son Eusebio Elacio, also an environmental defender, had been killed in 2018.

name: Raymundo Robles Riaño
summary: Raymundo Robles Riaño was shot dead in Barrio Chico, Paso de la Reina, Oaxaca on 14 March 2021 while on duty as an alternate community police officer. He was killed alongside Noé Robles Cruz and Gerardo Mendoza Reyes, and the assailants were never identified. He was a peasant farmer and community police officer who defended Paso de la Reina against a hydroelectric project on the Río Verde.

name: Grisell Pérez Rivera
summary: Grisell Pérez Rivera was disappeared on 26 March 2021. Her body was found in March 2022, but the remains were not forensically identified as Rivera until November 2022. Rivera was an advocate for women's rights and the founder of a women's shelter in Tlalmanalco, State of Mexico called Cabaña de la Sabiduría.

name: José de Jesús Sánchez García
summary: José de Jesús Sánchez García was reported missing and found dead a week later, on 23 March 2021. He was a park guard at Lagunas de Zempoala National Park who worked in defence of its forest lands; staff there had previously complained that their security conditions were inadequate.

name: Jaime Jiménez Ruiz
summary: Jaime Jiménez Ruiz was murdered by unidentified attackers on the road from Santiago Jamiltepec to Paso de la Reina, Oaxaca on 28 March 2021. He was a member of the Paso de la Reina ejido and an active member of the Council of United Peoples for the Defense of the Verde River, and had spoken about his community's experience at national and regional forums.

name: Carlos Marques Oyorzabal
summary: Carlos Marques Oyorzabal was kidnapped by unidentified aggressors on the night of 3 April 2021 while travelling with his two sons to Ciénega de Puerto Alegre, Guerrero. He was subjected to physical and psychological torture and a ransom was demanded. Oyorzabal was found dead the following day, dismembered and bearing signs of torture. He was a peasant farmer, ejido commissioner and community police member in Las Conchitas, defending forest land against clandestine logging.

name: José Santos Isaac Chávez
summary: José Santos Isaac Chávez was found dead in his car in Ayotitlán, Jalisco, on 4 April 2021. In the early hours of the previous day, armed men had come to his home claiming to be from the Attorney General's Office, harassed his wife and children, and taken him away handcuffed in his own vehicle. He was an active member of the Ayotitlán ejido and a candidate for ejido commissioner who had denounced environmental damage by the Peña Colorada mining project.

name: Blanca Estela Beltrán
summary: Blanca Estela Beltrán Segura was shot several times and her body dumped in the Tanamá area of Tecate, Baja California, where it was found on the afternoon of 19 April 2021. She was a community organiser and a member of the Movimiento Ciudadano party.

name: José de Jesús Robledo Cruz
summary: José de Jesús Robledo Cruz was found dead with his wife, María de Jesús Gómez Vega, on 30 April 2021 in Puerto Peñasco, Sonora. He chaired the commissariat of the El Bajío ejido in Caborca municipality and was a member of REMA, resisting mineral extraction by the Penmont mining company. In more than 18 years of activism he had been disappeared, threatened, harassed and physically attacked.

name: María de Jesús Gómez Vega
summary: María de Jesús Gómez Vega was found dead alongside her husband, José de Jesús Robledo Cruz, on 30 April 2021 in Puerto Peñasco, Sonora. An ejido member and environmental defender from Puerto Peñasco, she had taken up the defense of land against the environmental damage and land appropriation of the Penmont mining company.

name: Homero Terán Vanoye
summary: Homero Terán Vanoye was shot dead in Campeche on 19 May 2021. He was one of the leaders of former Oceanografía SA workers, who have been fighting a labor lawsuit against the shipping company for more than seven years.

name: Marco Antonio Arcos
summary: Marco Antonio Arcos was shot multiple times by a group of armed men in Chilpancingo, Guerrero on 21 May 2021. He was ejido commissioner in Jaleaca de Catalán and defended the forest of the Sierra de Chilpancingo against clandestine logging.

name: Francisco Javier Barajas Piña
summary: Francisco Javier Barajas Piña was murdered in Salvatierra, Guanajuato on 29 May 2021. He was an official of the Guanajuato Search Commission after his sister disappeared in February 2019 .

name: José Ascensión Carrillo Vázquez
summary: José Ascensión Carrillo Vázquez disappeared and was found dead a week later on 6 June 2021 alongside eight other people. Vázquez's body showed signs of physical assault and gunshot wounds. Also known as Don Chon, Vázquez defended water, land, and territory against the extractive operations of the Peñasquito mine in Mazapil. He had received several threats in 2020 and had asked the National Commission on Human Rights for protection without ever receiving a reply.

name: Luis Urbano Domínguez Mendoza
summary: Luis Urbano Domínguez Mendozawas shot dead by unidentified armed assailants as he was leaving a cash machine in downtown Cajeme, Sonora on 8 June 2021. A Yaqui water defender from Loma de Guamúchil, he had campaigned since 2012 for the biocultural heritage of the Yaqui Nation against massive infrastructure projects, among them the Independencia Water Pipeline.

name: Manuel Hidalgo Vázquez
summary: Manuel Hidalgo Vázquez was ambushed with Marco Antonio Jiménez de la Torre and Rolando Pérez González, and shot dead by members of the San Bartolomé de Los Llanos Alliance in Venustiano Carranza, Chiapas on 12 June 2021. He was a member of the Emiliano Zapata Peasant Organization–People's House (OCEZ-CP).

name: Marco Antonio Jiménez de la Torre
summary: Marco Antonio Jiménez de la Torre was ambushed with Manuel Hidalgo Vázquez and Rolando Pérez González and shot dead by members of the San Bartolomé de Los Llanos Alliance in Venustiano Carranza, Chiapas on 12 June 2021. He was a member of the Emiliano Zapata Peasant Organization–People's House (OCEZ-CP).

name: Rolando Pérez González
summary: Rolando Pérez González was ambushed with Manuel Hidalgo Vázquez and Marco Antonio Jiménez de la Torre and shot dead by members of the San Bartolomé de Los Llanos Alliance in Venustiano Carranza, Chiapas on 12 June 2021. He was a member of the Emiliano Zapata Peasant Organization–People's House (OCEZ-CP).

name: Tomás Rojo Valencia
summary: Tomás Rojo Valencia disappeared on 27 May 2021 while walking near his home and was found dead two weeks later on 17 June at a clandestine burial site in Vícam, Guaymas, Sonora. A Yaqui defender of water and territory, he was one of the leading opponents of the Independencia Water Pipeline and had been a victim of intimidation and harassment for years.

name: Federico de Jesús Gutiérrez
summary: Federico de Jesús Gutiérrez, a Triqui member of the Triqui Unification and Struggle Movement (MULT), was killed on the street in Santiago Juxtlahuaca, Oaxaca on 23 June 2021.

name: Flor de Jesús Hernández
summary: Flor de Jesús Hernández was murdered on 28 June 2021 with her husband, Oliverio Martínez Merino, while on her way to advise her students in the community of Coyuchi Copala, Santiago Juxtlahuaca, Oaxaca. She was a teacher and a member of the MULT.

name: Oliverio Martínez Merino
summary: Oliverio Martínez Merino was murdered on 28 June 2021 with his wife, Flor de Jesús Hernández, while on his way to advise his students in the community of Coyuchi Copala, Santiago Juxtlahuaca, Oaxaca. He was a teacher and a member of the MULT.

name: David Díaz Valdez
summary: David Díaz Valdez was shot several times by unidentified assailants on 2 July 2021, eleven days after his release from prison. A social activist opposing the environmental damage caused by a thermoelectric station in Manzanillo, he had been criminalised in September 2020 and imprisoned at the Chandiablo correctional facility. In February 2021 he said he feared for his life and held state authorities responsible for his safety.

name: Simón Pedro Pérez López
summary: Simón Pedro Pérez López was murdered on 5 July 2021 in his community in Pantelhó, Chiapas. A pacifist and catechist, he was a member of the civil society organisation Las Abejas de Acteal and president of its Board of Directors in 2020, aiding victims of the Acteal massacre and opposing forced displacement, militarisation and the imposition of infrastructure projects on Indigenous territory in Chiapas. Days before he was killed, López denounced the climate of aggression his community was suffering at the hands of organised crime.

name: Fabian Shadow Miranda
summary: Fabian Shadow Miranda was kidnapped along with 14 other people on 14 July 2021. Authorities in Sonora reported finding his remains, but search groups doubt the veracity of that account. Yaqui tribe, whose members attribute the disappearances to pressure from mining interests in collusion with the authorities, due to the Yaqui resistance to a local project.

name: Fabian Valencia Romero
summary: Fabian Valencia Romero was kidnapped along with 14 other people on 14 July 2021. Authorities in Sonora reported finding his remains, but search groups doubt the veracity of that account. Yaqui tribe, whose members attribute the disappearances to pressure from mining interests in collusion with the authorities, due to the Yaqui resistance to a local project.

name: Heladio Molina Zavala

Yaqui tribe, whose members attribute the disappearances to pressure from mining interests in collusion with the authorities, due to the Yaqui resistance to a local project.

summary: Juan Justino Galaviz Cruz was kidnapped along with 14 other people on 14 July 2021. Authorities in Sonora reported finding his remains, but search groups doubt the veracity of that account. Yaqui tribe, whose members attribute the disappearances to pressure from mining interests in collusion with the authorities, due to the Yaqui resistance to a local project.

summary: Martín Hurtado Flores was kidnapped along with 14 other people on 14 July 2021. Authorities in Sonora reported finding his remains, but search groups doubt the veracity of that account. Yaqui tribe, whose members attribute the disappearances to pressure from mining interests in collusion with the authorities, due to the Yaqui resistance to a local project.

name: Gladys Aranza Ramos Gurrola
summary: Gladys Aranza Ramos Gurrola was shot dead in her home in Sonora om 15 July 2021. She was an activist for families whose loved ones have been disappeared. Her husband was the victim of enforced disappearance.

name: Aline Sánchez
summary: Aline Sánchez was killed in Mexicaltzingo, State of Mexico on 19 July 2021. Her throat was cut. She was an advocate for transgender rights and a member of the Colectivo Mujeres Trans Famosas Toluca, and worked with LGBTQ+ people seeking to recover from addiction.

name: Román Rubio López
summary: Román Rubio López was abducted on the night of 20 July 2021 and killed by an armed group in Sinaloa de Leyva. His body was found on the bank of the Sinaloa river. A teacher, López led the Colectivo Tarahumara Sinaloense, which supports Rarámuri migrant families in Sinaloa. He belonged to the CNTE teachers' union.

name: José Nicanor Araiza Dávila
summary: José Nicanor Araiza Dávila was abducted on 22 July 2021 and found dead in El Durazno, Zacatecas. He was an advocate for families whose families experienced enforced disappearances, and worked with collectives of relatives of the disappeared in Zacatecas. Dávila never stopped searching for his own son, who disappeared in 2018.

name: Ramiro Ventura Apolonio
summary: Ramiro Ventura Apolonio was shot dead on his way home in Apanhuac, Acapulco, Guerrero on 3 August 2021. He was a member of the Council of Ejidos and Communities Opposed to the La Parota Dam (CECOP), and Regional Coordinator of Community Authorities (CRAC) of San Luis. Apolonio was a water defender opposed to the La Parota dam project on the Papagayo River.

name: Lea Juárez Valenzuela
summary: Lea Juárez Valenzuela was shot dead in the municipality of Candelaria, Campeche on 8 August 2021. She was the leader of an irregular settlement known as La Beraca, and was an advocate for farmers against rancher incursion. In February 2020, 16 homes in the community she led were burned down by the same armed group that killed her.

name: Hortensia Hernández Mendoza
summary: Hortensia Hernández Mendoza was shot dead in her home in eastern Tijuana, Baja California on 10 August 2021. She was a social leader in Maclovio Rojas.

name: Rodrigo Morales Vázquez
summary: Rodrigo Morales Vázquez was shot dead on 2 September 2021 in Cuernavaca, Morelos. An environmental activist and defender of water and of the Chichinautzin Biological Corridor against pollution, he created a waste collection centre in Cuernavaca and opposed the reopening of the Loma de Mejía landfill run by the companies Trideza and KS. He had previously been illegally detained and physically assaulted in 2008 in reprisal for his activism.

name: Manuel Cartas Pérez
summary: Manuel Cartas Pérez was shot dead in a motorcycle drive-by attack at a warehouse in the workshops district of Huatulco, Oaxaca on 3 September 2021. He was a member of the state committee of the Popular Revolutionary Front (FPR), which defended land and territory in Huatulco against tourist development projects.

name: Devanny Cardiel
summary: Devanny Cardiel was shot dead on 5 September 2021 inside her beauty salon in the Paseos del Molino neighbourhood of León, Guanajuato. She was a transgender rights activist and the trans ambassador for the state of Guanajuato and Miss Trans, and campaigned against the violence faced by trans and LGBTIQ+ communities.

name: Alejandro García Zagal
summary: Alejandro García Zagal was shot dead  at his home in Cuernavaca, Morelos on 7 September 2021. A photographer, water defender, and social activist campaigning for Cuernavaca residents' right to water, he had survived a shooting in 2020 and had demanded that the authorities investigate a Cuernavaca councilwoman who had threatened him.

name: Jacinto Hernández Quiroz
summary: Jacinto Hernández Quiroz disappeared on 1 October 2021; he was found dead with gunshot wounds two days later at the locality of Yu Kunu. He was a member of the community of Guerrero Grande, which has historically defended its forests against illegal logging.

name: Nayeli Guerrero
summary: Nayeli Guerrero went missing on 14 October 2021; her body was found days later showing signs of violence and strangulation in Baja California Sur. She was an animal rights activist.

name: Isidoro Hernández
summary: Isidoro Hernández was killed during attacks between 21 and 23 October 2021 by a group purportedly commanded by municipal authorities against the communities of Ndoyonoyuji, Guerrero Grande, and Mier y Terán. His body bore signs of gunshot wounds and torture. His identity was confirmed on 26 October by the Oaxaca State Attorney General's Office. He was an Indigenous defender of the San Esteban Atatlahuca forests.

name: Narciso López Vásquez
summary: Narciso López Vásquez was ambushed and killed on 28 October 2021. Oaxaca. A Tacuate Indigenous leader, he was alternate secretary of the Ixtayutla Communal Land Commission.

name: Jesus Solórzano Diaz
summary: Jesús Solórzano Díaz was killed in Chiapas on 7 November 2021. He was a member of the Emiliano Zapata-Carranza Region Peasant Organization (OCEZ-RC) and OCEZ-Casa del Pueblo.

name: Marisol Cuadras
summary: Marisol Cuadras was shot and killed during a peaceful demonstration with the Feministas del Mar collective on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women in Guayma, Sonora on 25 November 2021.

name: Marcelino Álvarez González
summary: Marcelino Álvarez González was murdered by two men while driving his vehicle in Oaxaca. González was a member of the Triqui Unification and Struggle Movement (MULT).

name: Rosendo Gonzalez Torres
summary: Rosendo González Torres and his 17-year-old grandson Estanislao were abducted from their home in the early hours of 7 January 2022. Their bodies were found the next day in a ravine on the outskirts of the community, both bound and bearing signs of torture and gunshot wounds. González Torres was a leader of traditional healers of the Wixárika people and a defender of sacred territory against attempts at appropriation by livestock and mining companies.

name: Mario Zamora Maldonado
summary: Mario Zamora Maldonado was killed in an ambush on 26 January 2022 by an armed group who attacked the base of the Union of Peoples and Organizations of the State of Guerrero. He was a member of the Guerrero State Coordinating Committee of Education Workers – National Coordinating Committee of Education Workers, and led the struggle of the State Coordinator of Education Workers of Guerrero (CETEG) against unpopular education reforms.

name: Ana Luisa Garduño Juárez
summary: Ana Luisa Garduño Juárez was shot three times in a bar on the night of 27 January 2022. She founded the collective Ana Karen Vive and had campaigned since 2012 for justice for the feminicide of her daughter, Ana Karen Huicochea, and for other victims of femicide in the state.

name: Moisés Álvarez Ramírez
summary: Moisés Álvarez Ramírez was beaten in Chiapas and died from the after-effects. He was a member of the Ejido of Tila.

name: Verónica Patricia Guerrero Vinueza
summary: Verónica Patricia Guerrero Vinueza was killed in an armed attack on 3 February 2022 in Tonalá, Jalisco. She campaigned against the irregular operation of the Coyula landfill, and campaigned for better waste management. Before her death, she had reported threats and attacks from waste collectors who opposed the landfill's closure.

name: Vera Aidee Varela Melgarejo
summary: Vera Aidee Varela Melgarejo was murdered with a bladed weapon in Quintana Roo on 5 February 2022. She was a member of the feminist collective Brujas del Mar.

name: Francisco Vazquez Dominguez
summary: Francisco Vázquez Domínguez was shot dead on 11 February 2022 on his own farmland, the day after he had publicly denounced death threats against him. He opposed the Morelos Integral Project, in particular the Huexca thermoelectric plant, because of its proposed use of water from the Cuautla River. He had led the legal defense against the project by filing constitutional appeals.

name: Jose Trinidad Baldenegro Lopez
summary: José Trinidad Baldenegro López was gunned down on 7 March 2022. Armed men then burned his house down. He was a defender of the forest and territory of Coloradas de la Virgen.

name: Patricia Susana Rivera Reyes
summary: Patricia Susana Rivera Reyes was killed by a gunshot to the head in her home on 19 March 2022. She was a lawyer and Indigenous rights defender, and founded the Indigenous Peoples' Consultancy in Northern Mexico.

name: Nestor Ivan Merino Flores
summary: Néstor Iván Merino Flores was shot and killed by two people on a motorcycle in the Cañada region of Oaxaca on the night of 20 March 2022. He led the Asamblea Popular de los Pueblos Indígenas and had reported death threats to the federal Interior Ministry and the state prosecutor's office, without being granted protective measures.

name: Julia Hernández García
summary: Julia Hernández García was murdered in her home in the Arboleda neighbourhood of Oaxaca City on 8 April 2022. She co-founded the Hermanos en Situación de Vulnerabilidad AC Foundation and provided in-kind support to vulnerable senior citizens and premature babies.

name: Hector Soto Rodriguez
summary: Héctor Soto Rodríguez was killed by unidentified armed men in Cuernavaca, Morelos, as he got into his truck on 19 April 2022. Considered by his colleagues one of the best agrarian lawyers in the country, he had won important cases protecting the environment and land from illegal appropriation. Members of NAAME said that in the months before his death, Rodríguez had received calls from a range of different numbers warning him to drop the cases he was working on.

name: Juana Ovando de los Santos
summary: Juana Ovando de los Santos was found dead in the bathroom of her home in the Guadalupe Rodríguez neighbourhood of Xalapa, Veracruz, on 20 April 2022, from blows to the head and body. She was a feminist activist who took part in women's marches and belonged to the youth wing of the PRI.

name: Silvestre Luciano Hernández
summary: Silvestre Luciano Hernández was murdered at the María del Carmen Serdán school in Oaxaca on 27 April 2022 during a community work day held ahead of the return to classes. He was the general secretary of Union Delegation DI-146 of the National Coordinator of Education Workers.

name: Luis Donato Ortiz
summary: Luis Donato Ortiz was shot dead by armed men on a ranch in Guerrero on 28 April 2022. He was the founder of the Marquelia Citizen Council, an organization for the rights of Afro-Mexican peoples in Guerrero and Oaxaca.

name: Lorenza Chantzin Paxacuasingo
summary: Lorenza Chantzin Paxacuasingo was detained and disappeared with Marcos Campos Ahuejote on 6 May 2022 at a highway crossing near Atzacualoya in Álvarez, Guerrero. Her body, showing signs of torture, was found on a stretch of the highway the next day. The Guerrero State Attorney General's Office claimed she died in an automobile accident. Paxacuasingo was an activist against the appropriation of her territory for mining.

name: Marcos Campos Ahuejote
summary: Marcos Campos Ahuejote was detained and disappeared with Lorenza Chantzin Paxacuasingo on 6 May 2022 at a highway crossing near Atzacualoya in Álvarez, Guerrero. His body, showing signs of torture, was found on a stretch of the highway the next day. The Guerrero State Attorney General's Office claimed he died in an automobile accident. He was an activist against the appropriation of his territory for mining.

name: Marcelo Carrera Reyes
summary: Marcelo Carrera Reyes was killed on 9 May 2022 with Marcelo Carrera Reyes and Teófilo Barrera Herrera when state police officers attacked a vehicle carrying them near the village of Cobatzalco, Puebla. Witnesses said the officers blocked their way and opened fire, wounding several people and killing the defenders. Nine state police officers were subsequently detained on charges of homicide, attempted homicide, and other offenses.

name: Omar Herrera Raymundo
summary: Omar Herrera Raymundo was killed on 9 May 2022 with Marcelo Carrera Reyes and Teófilo Barrera Herrera when state police officers attacked a vehicle carrying them near the village of Cobatzalco, Puebla. Witnesses said the officers blocked their way and opened fire, wounding several people and killing the defenders. Nine state police officers were subsequently detained on charges of homicide, attempted homicide, and other offenses.

name: Teófilo Barrera Herrera
summary: Teófilo Barrera Herrera was killed on 9 May 2022 with Marcelo Carrera Reyes and Omar Herrera Raymundo when state police officers attacked a vehicle carrying them near the village of Cobatzalco, Puebla. Witnesses said the officers blocked their way and opened fire, wounding several people and killing the defenders. Nine state police officers were subsequently detained on charges of homicide, attempted homicide, and other offenses.

name: Cecilia Monzón
summary: Cecilia Monzón was shot dead by two men as she drove her car in San Pedro Cholula, Puebla on 21 May 2022. She was a lawyer specialising in gender issues and a feminist activist who represented women who had suffered domestic violence. Her former partner, the ex-legislator Javier López Zavala, was later sentenced to 60 years in prison for ordering her murder.

name: Humberto Valdovinos Fuentes
summary: Humberto Valdovinos Fuentes was killed by armed individuals in Oaxaca on 23 May 2022. He was a peasant leader and Indigenous land defender.

name: Noe Godinez Arredondo
summary: Noé Godínez Arredondo was reported missing on 18 May 2022; he was discovered dead six days later with signs of torture and bullet wounds. He was a lawyer and representative of Ejido Property of San Francisco Uruapan.

name: Camila Boloca
summary: Camila Boloca was found dead in her Mexico City apartment on 4 June 2022. Her body showed signs of torture. Originally from Chile, she was a transgender activist, and member of the Amanda Jofré Chilean Corporation of Trans People, an organization dedicated to the defense of the human rights of trans women and sex workers.

name: Paulino Durán Flores
summary: Paulino Durán Flores was stabbed to death in Cherán, Michoacán on 14 June 2022. He was an Indigenous Purépecha community member, and a land defender.

name: Pedro Vásquez Ramírez
beat: Community leader and head of the Council of Indigenous Communities of the Loxicha and Sierra Sur Region (CCIRLSS) and former municipal president of San Agustín Loxicha.
summary: Pedro Vásquez Ramírez was shot dead in Oaxaca on 14 June 2022. Ramírez was the former mayor of San Agustín Loxicha, Oaxaca, and was a community leader known for his fight against groups that oppressed citizens. He was the leader of the Council of Indigenous Communities of the Loxicha and Sierra Sur Region (CCIRLSS), and had formerly received threats and feared for his life and that of his family.

name: Antonio Mérida
summary: Antonio Mérida was shot dead from a moving motorcycle in Veracruz on 17 June 2022. He was a vendor at the San Andrés Tuxtla market, and president of the Committee Against the New February 5th Market. The crime occurred amidst a months-long conflict between market vendors and the municipal administration.

name: Fernando Guerrero Pérez
summary: Fernando Guerrero Pérez was reported missing on 16 June 2022 in Papantla, Veracruz; he found dead the next day, his naked body bearing signs of torture and stab wounds. Pérez was an activist for the LGBTQ+ community.

name: Jesus Banuelos Acevedo
summary: Jesús Bañuelos Acevedo was shot in the head in the early hours of 20 June 2022 while protesting against the operation of the Atitalaquia Regional Urban Solid Waste Treatment Centre in Hidalgo. He had focused his work on opposing a new sanitary landfill in Atitalaquia, a hazardous waste discharge zone that had been in operation for more than forty years. Other environmental defenders at the sit-in were wounded in the same attack, in which armed assailants used firearms, metal pipes and sticks.

name: Joaquin Cesar Mora Salazar
summary: Joaquín César Mora Salazar, a Jesuit priest, was shot dead inside a church in Urique, Chihuahua, on 20 June 2022. A second priest and advocate, Javier Campos Morales, was murdered with him. For more than 30 years, Salazar had ministered to Indigenous communities in the mountains of Chihuahua, working in defence of the rights of Indigenous peoples from Sisoguichi to Cerocahui.

name: Elodia Mateos Gutiérrez
summary: Elodia Mateos Gutiérrez was shot dead in Baja, California on 22 June 2022. She was a community leader and social activist in the town of Maclovio Rojas.

name: Alberto Morales Sebastian
summary: Alberto Morales Sebastián was shot dead on 9 July 2022 after travelling to Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero, to receive medical care. He was shot while waiting for public transport after leaving the hospital. He was a member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero-Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ).

name: Crispín Reyes Pablo
summary: Crispín Reyes Pablo was shot and killed while working on a property near the community of Juquila Mixes on 14 July 2014. He was a community representative and advocate for families who were forcibly displaced from their communities of origin.

name: Brenda Jazmín Beltrán Jaime
summary: Brenda Jazmín Beltrán Jaime was strangled to death in Sonora on 17 July 2022. She was an advocate for families of the disappeared, and had been searching for her disappeared brother since 2018.

name: Álvaro Sebastián Ramírez
beat: Zapotec, Oaxaca.  Teacher, former political prisoner, defender of the rights of the peoples of San Agustín Loxicha, adherent to the Sixth Declaration of the Lacandon Jungle, lifelong social fighter .
summary: Álvaro Sebastián Ramírez was shot dead on the afternoon of 19 July 2022 at his home on the edge of Oaxaca City. A Zapotec teacher and community leader from San Agustín Loxicha, he spent almost twenty years in prison accused of taking part in a 1996 armed attack by the Ejército Popular Revolucionario, was released in 2017, and returned to organising in defence of the Loxicha communities and of other former political prisoners.

name: Efraín González
summary: Efraín González was murdered with two relatives by a group of hitmen who stormed his home in La Rosita, Zacatecas on 19 July 2022. A Wixárika artisan and musician, González belonged to a family that defends the rights of the Wixárika people.

name: Luz Raquel Padilla
summary: Luz Raquel Padilla was burned alive in Zapopan, Jalisco. She was an advocate for people with disabilities, and had an autistic son with high care needs.

name: Eloy Merino Mendoza
summary: Eloy Merino Mendoza was killed in an ambush in Puebla along with five others on 20 July 2022. He led the self-defense group Fuerza Territorial Poblana.

name: Nicolas Perez Xoyateco
summary: Nicolás Pérez Xoyateco was shot dead on 24 July 2022 in Chilapa, Guerrero. He was a member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero-Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ).

name: Rosario Lilián Rodríguez Barraza
summary: Rosario Lilián Rodríguez Barraza was murdered in the municipality of Elota, Sinaloa. She was a member of the “Hearts Without Justice” collective, helping search for the disappeared after her son was disappeared in 2019.

name: Eusebio Fragoso Faranoni
summary: Eusebio Fragoso Faranoni was shot dead by two men in the State of Mexico on 8 September 2022. He was an activist and social leader.

name: Susana Villarreal
summary: Susana Villarreal was murdered in Durango on 14 September 2022. Her body showed signs of physical and sexual violence. She was a transgender rights activist.

name: Isabella Álvarez
beat: Unsure if activist
summary: Isabella Álvarez was murdered by strangulation in Guanajuato on 29 September 2022. She was a transgender rights activist.

name: Rosa Salvaje
summary: Rosa Salvaje was shot dead in her business in Oaxaca on 29 September 2022. She was a transgender rights advocate and political activist.

name: Julio Isidro Ramírez González
summary: Julio Isidro Ramírez González was killed when his vehicle was attacked by paramilitaries in Oaxaca on 1 October 2022. He was a member of the Independent Triqui Unification and Struggle Movement (MULTI).

name: Blanca Esmeralda Gallardo
summary: Blanca Esmeralda Gallardo was shot dead by two people in the city of Puebla on 4 October 2022. She was a member of the Voice of the Disappeared collective and an advocate for families with disappeared loved ones, after her daughter was disappeared in 2021. Gallardo had previously requested enrollment in the federal protection mechanism, and was denied.

name: Beatriz Rojas Pérez
beat: Student teacher at the Benito Juárez Rural Teachers' College  in Panotla, Tlaxcala.
summary: Beatriz Rojas Pérez died as a result of an attack by police on a demonstration by student teachers in Tlaxcala on 22 October 2022. She was a teacher.

name: Gulliermo Álvaro López
beat: San Isidro de Morelos, Putla de Guerrero, Oaxaca. Teacher at Technical Secondary School No. 32 of San Pedro y San Pablo Teposcolula.  Member of the delegation committee of Delegation D-II-38 of Technical Secondary Schools, Tlaxiaco Sector of Section XXII – of the National Coordinator of Education Workers (CNTE) .
summary: Guillermo Álvaro López was reported missing on 23 October 2022; his body was found two days later showing signs of violence, at the bottom of a ravine. He was a history teacher at Technical Secondary School No. 32 in San Pedro y San Pablo Teposcolula, and sat on the committee of delegation D-II-38 of the CNTE teachers' union Section 22.

name: Filogonio Martinez Merino
summary: Filogonio Martínez Merino was the victim of an armed assault on 26 October 2022. A former municipal agent and former ejido commissioner of Paso de la Reyna, he had defended the Río Verde against hydroelectric projects for 15 years. He was enrolled in preventive measures granted by the Protection Mechanism for Human Rights Defenders and Journalists.

name: Jesus Manuel Garcia Martinez
summary: Jesús Manuel García Martínez was murdered on 27 October 2022 when an armed group attacked his home in Santo Domingo Tehuantepec, Oaxaca. He was a member of the social organisation Corriente del Pueblo Sol Rojo, a land defender, and an opponent of the Interoceanic Corridor.

name: Renata Nicole Duarte Reyes
summary: Renata Nicole Duarte Reyes was shot dead in Morelos along with another trans woman on 4 November 2022. The two women were found dead and bound. Reyes was a transgender rights activist and the founder of the Cuautla Diversity Collective. She organized health fairs in her municipality, offered STI testing, and gave empowerment workshops for trans women, domestic workers, and sex workers.

name: Adan Linares Silverio
summary: Adán Linares Silverio was detained on Saturday 5 November 2022 in Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero by men presumed to be municipal traffic police. They took him and two fellow defenders to an undisclosed location. Their bodies were found that night in the community of Xochimilco. Two weeks earlier, on 21 October, Silverio had read a statement to President López Obrador denouncing the harassment his community suffered from criminal groups. He was under protective measures ordered by the Mechanism for Protection of Defenders and Journalists when he was killed. He was a member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ) and of the CRAC Founding Peoples community police (CRAC-PF).

name: Guillermo Hilario Morales
summary: Guillermo Hilario Morales was detained on Saturday 5 November 2022 in Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero by men presumed to be municipal traffic police. They took him and two fellow defenders to an undisclosed location. Their bodies were found that night in the community of Xochimilco. He was the brother of Pablo Hilario Morales, missing since 25 January 2022. He was a member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ) and of the CRAC Founding Peoples community police (CRAC-PF).

name: Moises Cuapipistenco
summary: Moisés Cuapipistenco was detained on Saturday 5 November 2022 in Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero by men presumed to be municipal traffic police. They took him and two fellow defenders to an undisclosed location. Their bodies were found that night in the community of Xochimilco. A promoter and farmer committed to spreading his culture and native language, he was a member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ) and of the CRAC Founding Peoples community police (CRAC-PF).

name: María Carmela Vázquez
summary: María Carmela Vázquez was shot dead at her home by two men in Abasolo, Guanajuato on 6 November 2022. She was a member of the collective Disappeared Persons of Pénjamo, Guanajuato, after her son was disappeared several months earlier.

name: Karen Sánchez Álvarez
beat: She was part of the State of Mexico Human Rights sports team, the State of Mexico & Surrounding Areas Collective, and the Realitrans AC collective.  She was an activist promoting sexual health and HIV/AIDS prevention .
summary: Karen Sánchez Álvarez was shot dead in Michoacán on 10 November 2022. She was a member of the Realitrans AC collective, a health promoter, and a transgender rights advocate.

name: Pedro Pascual Cruz
summary: Pedro Pascual Cruz was shot dead by armed men on 10 December 2022. He was a defender of the Ocumicho forests, and coordinator of the Community Patrol of Ocumicho.

name: José Rubén Cruz Palma
summary: José Rubén Cruz Palma was murdered along with his wife on the highway to Hermosillo on 11 December 2022. He was the traditional authority of the Yaqui people of Belem, Sonora.

name: José Francisco Zapata Alvarado
summary: José Francisco Zapata Alvarado was killed in an armed attack while changing a tire in Zacatecas on 14 December 2022. He was a young left-wing student activist in Zacatecas.

name: Francisco Jiménez López
beat: Member of the Popular Revolutionary Front (FPR) , in Nochixtlán, Oaxaca
summary: Francisco Jiménez López was run over and killed by an unmarked vehicle that rammed a roadblock while he was demonstrating against the arrest of a colleague on 19 December 2022. He was a member of the Popular Revolutionary Front (FPR) in Oaxaca.

name: Ana Cristina García
summary: Ana Cristina García was shot in the head on 8 August 2022 during an ambush in the municipality of Santiago Juxtlahuaca. She died of her injuries on 20 December 2022. She was a Triqui woman and member of the MULT in Putla Villa de Guerrero, Oaxaca.

name: Remigio de la Cruz López
summary: Remigio de la Cruz López was shot on the night of 1 January 2023 in Zacualpan, in the municipality of Ometepec, Guerrero. An Amuzgo (Nomndaa) catechist, he sat on the committee promoting a justice and development plan for the Amuzga Nation. Days earlier, López had publicly asked his parish to pray for him, because he was receiving death threats.

name: Isaúl Nemesio Zambrano
beat: Member of the community guard of Santa María Ostula, Aquila, Michoacán.
summary: Isaúl Nemesio Zambrano was killed at a checkpoint near the municipal seat of Aquila, Michoacán on 12 January 2023 with Rolando Magno Zambrano and Miguel Estrada Reyes. The defenders were killed while patrolling and protecting communal territory, and were members of the Communal Guard of Santa María Ostula. Their community was resisting pressure to expand a mining project.

name: Miguel Estrada Reyes
summary: Miguel Estrada Reyes was killed at a checkpoint near the municipal seat of Aquila, Michoacán on 12 January 2023 with Isaúl Nemesio Zambrano and Rolando Magno Zambrano. The defenders were killed while patrolling and protecting communal territory, and were members of the Communal Guard of Santa María Ostula. Their community was resisting pressure to expand a mining project.

name: Rolando Magno Zambrano
summary: Rolando Magno Zambrano, was killed at a checkpoint near the municipal seat of Aquila, Michoacán on 12 January 2023 with Miguel Estrada Reyes and Isaúl Nemesio Zambrano. The defenders were killed while patrolling and protecting communal territory, and were members of the Communal Guard of Santa María Ostula. Their community was resisting pressure to expand a mining project.

name: Mayolo Quiroz Barrios
summary: Mayolo Quiroz Barrios disappeared at about 5 a.m. on 10 October 2021; his remains were discovered on 13 January 2022. He was a defender of the forest of Mier y Terán, San Esteban Atatlahuca, in a conflict in which municipal authorities were implicated under provisional measures ordered by the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights.

name: Constantino Silvestre Pacheco Luis
summary: Constantino Silvestre Pacheco Luis was shot and killed by two armed men on 12 January 2023. He was a Zapotec leader of the Council of Indigenous Communities of the Loxicha Region and Sierra Sur of Oaxaca.

name: Juan Martínez Flores
summary: Juan Martínez Flores was shot and killed in Santiago Juxtlahuaca, Oaxaca on 28 January 2023. He was a Triqui man and member of the Triqui Unification and Struggle Movement (MULT).

name: Gabina De Jesús Martínez
summary: Gabina de Jesús Martínez was killed in Santiago Juxtlahuaca, Oaxaca on 9 February 2023 with María Ramírez Martínez and Leodegario Cruz de Jesús. The three defenders were traveling in a car when they were ambushed before arriving at the Concepción Carrizal Community. She was a Triqui woman and member of the Triqui Unification and Struggle Movement (MULT).

name: Leodegario Cruz de Jesús
summary: Leodegario Cruz de Jesús was killed in Santiago Juxtlahuaca, Oaxaca on 9 February 2023 with María Ramírez Martínez and Gabina De Jesús Martínez. The three defenders were traveling in a car when they were ambushed before arriving at the Concepción Carrizal Community. He was a Triqui man and member of the Triqui Unification and Struggle Movement (MULT).

name: María Ramírez Martínez
summary: María Ramírez Martínez was killed in Santiago Juxtlahuaca, Oaxaca on 9 February 2023 with Gabina De Jesús Martínez and Leodegario Cruz de Jesús. The three defenders were traveling in a car when they were ambushed before arriving at the Concepción Carrizal Community. She was a Triqui woman and member of the Triqui Unification and Struggle Movement (MULT).

name: Alfredo Cisneros Madrigal
summary: Alfredo Cisneros Madrigal was killed by armed men in his home in Los Reyes, Michoacán on 21 February 2023. An Indigenous leader, defender of the Purépecha forests and promoter of Purépecha autonomy, he had been elected president of the Communal Property Commission of Sicuicho five months earlier and had reported illegal logging in the pine forests to the authorities.

name: Martiniano De Jesús Osorio
summary: Martiniano de Jesús Osorio was shot dead in Rosario, Oaxaca on 27 March 2023. He was found in his truck. Osorio was a Triqui community leader and member the Triqui Unified Struggle Movement (MULT).

name: Gustavo Robles Taboada
beat: Gustavo was a promoter of education and against homophobic discourse in that region of the state and worked as a stylist and official in the Ayala City Council, as director of Tourism, the fact has caused shock and indignation among members of the community and other groups.
summary: Gustavo Robles Taboada was murdered in his car by a motorcyclist in Morelos on 28 March 2023. He was a teacher, LGBTQ+ activist, and official of the Ayala City Council.

name: Eustacio Alcala Diaz
summary: Eustacio Alcalá Díaz was abducted 1 April 2023 while driving a group of nuns along the road from Huitzontla to the Coalcomán federal highway in Michoacán; he was found dead three days later. He was an Indigenous land defender who had pursued legal action against mining operations in his community of San Juan Huitzontla and had succeeded in stopping mining projects.

name: Felix Vicente Cruz
summary: Félix Vicente Cruz was shot and killed while leaving his place of work in San Francisco Ixhuatán, Oaxaca on 13 April 2023. He was a Zapotec defender and head of the municipal administration in San Francisco Ixhuatán. Cruz opposed the Interoceanic Corridor project and had taken part in roadblocks days before his killing as part of a National Indigenous Resistance Campaign.

name: Juan Medina
summary: Juan Medina as killed in an armed assault while working at a restaurant in Chinicuila, Michoacán on 14 April 2023. A Nahua man, he was a communal leader, a former chief tenancy officer, a communal guard and an active member of the Commission on Communication of Santa María Ostula.

name: Teresa Magueyal Ramírez
beat: Searching mother and member of the collective “A Promise to Fulfill”, San Miguel Octopan, Guanajuato.
summary: Teresa Magueyal Ramírez was shot by two men on motorcycles on the street in Celaya, Guanajuato on 2 May 2023. The perpetrators watched Ramírez running errands, and shot her in the chest and head. She was part of the collective Una promesa por cumplir, a group of relatives of victims of enforced disappearances. Her son was disappeared in April 2020.

name: Hortensia Felipe Santiago
summary: Hortensia Felipe Santiago was shot to death on the night of 3 May 2023 while walking to San Agustín Loxhicha, Oaxaca. She was a member of the Council of Indigenous Communities of the Loxicha and Sierra Sur Region (CCIRLSS).

name: Esthela Guadalupe Estrada Ávila
summary: Esthela Guadalupe Estrada Ávila was abducted from her home on 29 March 2023 and found dead on 4 June 2023 inside a clandestine grave in Tlajomulco, Jalisco. She was an advocate for families whose loved ones had been forcibly disappeared, after her brother was disappeared in February 2020.

name: Cuauhtemoc Marquez Fernandez
summary: Cuauhtémoc Márquez Fernández was attacked in his home in Tlalmanalco, State of Mexico, and died at the Zentlalpan hospital in Amecameca on 12 June 2023. A researcher in agroecology and apiculture, he advocated for better water management and campaigned for a new General Water Act.

name: Gertrudis Cruz de Jesús
summary: Gertrudis Cruz de Jesús was ambushed and shot dead at El Hongo, Yosoyuxi, Oaxaca on 15 June 2023 with Cliserina Cruz Merino while the two were travelling in a vehicle of the state prosecutor's office to seek medical attention. A Triqui teacher, she was an activist of the Movimiento de Unificación y Lucha Triqui (MULT).

name: Álvaro Arvizu Aguiñiga
summary: Álvaro Arvizu Aguiñiga was shot in the early hours of 13 June 2023 in the Centli Centre in Tlalmanalco, State of Mexico, and died of his injuries on 19 June. The assailants also threatened his wife and colleagues. He was an activist against the exploitation of water by transnational corporations and worked with the Incalli Ixcahuicopa Centre for Sustainability (CENTLI).

name: Cliserina Cruz Merino
summary: Cliserina Cruz Merino was ambushed and shot dead at El Hongo, Yosoyuxi, Oaxaca on 15 June 2023 with Gertrudis Cruz de Jesús while the two were travelling in a vehicle of the state prosecutor's office to seek medical attention. A Triqui teacher, she was an activist of the Movimiento de Unificación y Lucha Triqui (MULT).

name: Hipólito Mora Chávez
summary: Hipólito Mora Chávez was killed along with his bodyguards while travelling in his vehicle in Michoacán on 29 June 2023. The attackers set the car on fire. He was a farmer and politician, and founded a vigilante self-defense group in his town of La Ruana in response to cartel activity in the region.

name: Manuel Flores Reyes
summary: Manuel Flores Reyes was shot dead on 4 July 2023, together with Román Flores Hernández, when gunmen serving a local leader opened fire on a plebiscite to appoint the justice of the peace of the Nahua community of Xacaxomulco, Quimixtlán, Puebla. He was a resident of Xacaxomulco taking part in the community's opposition to the local leader, whose community that had seized control of a local spring.

name: Noel Lopez Gallegos
summary: Noel López Gallegos was reported missing on 3 July 2023 and found dead in a vacant lot in Santa María Mixtequilla on the Isthmus of Tehuantepec, Oaxaca. A member of Resistencia Civil Pacífica, he opposed the expropriation of land for an industrial park linked to the Interoceanic Corridor of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec.

name: Roman Flores Hernandez
summary: Román Flores Hernández was shot dead on 4 July 2023, together with Manuel Flores Reyes, when gunmen serving a local leader opened fire on a plebiscite to appoint the justice of the peace of the Nahua community of Xacaxomulco, Quimixtlán, Puebla. He was a resident of Xacaxomulco taking part in the community's opposition to the local leader, whose community that had seized control of a local spring.

name: Ulises Salvador Nava Juárez
summary: Ulises Salvador Nava Juárez was shot at least nine times at point-blank range by a man who then fled on a motorcycle outside of the Descubre museum in Aguascalientes on 17 July 2023. Juárez was shot as he left the First National Congress of Strategic Litigation for the Defence of the Rainbow Quota. He was an LGBTQ+ rights activist and head of the Department of Sexual Diversity at the Autonomous University of Guerrero (UAGro).

name: Gregorio de la Cruz de la Cruz
summary: Gregorio de la Cruz de la Cruz was found dead with stab wounds to his face and signs of torture in Chalma, Veracruz on 23 July 2023. He was a Nahua member of the National Front for the Struggle of Socialism (FNLS) and the Eastern Democratic Front of Mexico Emiliano Zapata (Fedomez). He was also the Ejidal commissioner of the indigenous town of Metlaltepec in the municipality of Huautla, Hidalgo.

name: Lorenzo Froylan de la Cruz Rios
summary: Lorenzo Froylán de la Cruz Ríos, was kidnapped on 1 August 2023 at a checkpoint set up by the Jalisco New Generation Cartel in Coalcomán, Michoacán; nine days later his body was found mutilated and bearing signs of torture on the Coalcomán–Aquila highway in Chinicuila. Ríos was a community activist and communal guard of Santa María Ostula,

name: Estaban Xochitempa Tepexco
beat: Nahua
summary: Estaban Xochitempa Tepexcowas murdered alongside his 16-year-old son near a petrol station in the municipality of Chilapa, Guerrero on 13 August 2023.  Tepexcowas was a member of the Emiliano Zapata Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero (CIPOG-EZ) from the community of Xochitempa.

name: Marcelino Hernandez Tecorral
summary: Marcelino Hernández Tecorral, was detained by armed and uniformed men on the highway between Chilpancingo and Chilapa, Guerrero, while returning from Sinaloa with two others on 17 August 2023. His body was found the same night in the municipality of Tixtla. Tecorral was a Nahua member of Indigenous and Popular Council-Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ). His companions Ángel Villalba Salvador and Nicolás Rodríguez Díaz, also CIPOG-EZ members, were disappeared.

name: Gloria Cañez Chávez
summary: Gloria Cañez Chávez was shot and killed with her daughter on 9 September 2023. They were found on a road in the Yerbabuena community, executed by more than 50 bullets. Chávez was killed by a criminal group disputing control of forestry operations in the area of Chihuahua where she lived. She was a longtime defender of the rights of the Rarámuri people, and worked to recover their land. Her husband, also a human rights defender, was killed in 2014.

name: Bonifacio Xochitempa Tlalxintli
summary: Bonifacio Xochitempa Tlalxintli was murdered by armed men at a bus stop in Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero on 12 September 2023. He was a member of CIPOG-EZ from the community of Xochitempa.

name: José Juan Hernández Fiscaleño
summary: José Juan Hernández Fiscaleño disappeared on 26 September 2023 while riding a motorcycle with his partner Albertha Santos Tomas; both bodies were found the next day near the entrance to San Jerónimo Palantla. A Nahua man from Alcozacán, he was a member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of the State of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ).

name: Albertha Santos Tomas
summary: Albertha Santos Tomas disappeared on 26 September 2023 while riding a motorcycle with her partner José Juan Hernández Fiscaleño; both bodies were found the next day near the entrance to San Jerónimo Palantla. A Nahua woman from Alcozacán, she was a member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of the State of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ).

name: Norberto Márquez Molina
summary: Norberto Márquez Molina was killed by a group of armed men in a resturaunt on 8 October 2023. He led the Civil Resistance to Non-Payment of Electricity group Costeños Unidos in Alto Lucero, Veracruz, advocating the Laguna Verde nuclear power plant pay for electricity for the communities it operates near.

name: Bruno Plácido Valerio
