summary: Bruno Plácido Valerio was shot dead, along with his driver, by armed men at the entrance to the Guerrero state health ministry in Chilpancingo on 17 October 2023. A Mixtec community leader, he founded and coordinated the Unión de Pueblos y Organizaciones del Estado de Guerrero (UPOEG) and was among the founders of the CRAC community police in 1995.

name: Jesús Toral García Rangel
summary: Jesús Toral García Rangel was shot and killed while driving on 21 October 2023. He was a Purépecha representative of communal property in Uruapan, Michoacán, and a member of Sector IX of Indigenous Education within the National Coordinator of Education Workers (CNTE).

name: José Artemio López Aguilar
summary: José Artemio López Aguilar was shot dead by armed men at his home in front of his family in Chicomuselo, Chiapas on 21 October 2023. A teacher and union leader, he had led the March for Peace in the municipality on 12 October 2023.

name: Jesús Ociel Baena Saucedo
summary: Jesús Ociel Baena Saucedo was found dead with razor wounds at their home in Aguascalientes alongside their partner on 13 November 2023. The state prosecutor's office concluded that the partner killed them and then took their own life, a finding activist groups have questioned. Baena had received death threats in the past. He was secretary of agreements acting as substitute magistrate at the Aguascalientes state electoral tribunal, an LGBTQ+ rights defender, and the first openly non-binary person to hold a judicial magistracy in Latin America.

name: Higinio Trinidad de la Cruz
summary: Higinio Trinidad de la Cruz was kidnapped as he left the municipal government offices there in Jalisco on 24 November 2023; his body was found one day later with signs of violence and a gunshot wound  in the town of Las Marías in the Ejido of Ayotitlán. Trinidad was a Nahua environmentalist from Cuautitlán de García Barragán. He defended the Sierra de Manantlán and the community of Ayotitlán against illegal mining and sat on the State Indigenous Council. He had been enrolled in Mexico's Protective Mechanism for Human Rights Defenders since 2021, and received constant threats.

name: Mario Reyes Ramírez
summary: Mario Reyes Ramírez was killed during an ambush in Santiago Juxtlahuaca, Oaxaca on 3 December 2023. A Triqui man and member of the Unifying Movement of the Triqui Struggle (MULT), the ambush occured in the place as the murder of two other MULT activists—Gertrudis Cruz de Jesús and Cliserina Cruz Merino—were murdered on June 15, 2023.

name: Humberto Cruz Ortiz
summary: Humberto Cruz Ortiz was killed in Santiago Juxtlahuaca, Oaxaca on 19 December 2023. He was a Triqui man and the leader of the Unifying Movement of the Triqui Struggle (MULT) Tierra Blanca.

name: Aronia Wilson Tambo
summary: Aronia Wilson Tambo was killed at her home in San Luis Río Colorado, Sonora on 10 January 2024. She was the traditional governor of the Cucapah people, one of the last speakers of the Cucapah language and a promoter and defender of its culture, and represented her people on the municipal council.

name: Miriam Ríos Ríos
summary: Miriam Ríos Ríos was shot dead in Michoacán on 11 January 2024. She was a transgender rights activist and a municipal leader of the Citizen Movement in Michoacán.

name: Carmen Lopez Lugo
summary: Carmen López Lugo was killed on the night of 12 January 2024 with 9-millimeter caliber weapons reported to be for the exclusive use of the Mexican Army. A member of the Chol indigenous community of Tila and of the National Indigenous Council, she served on the oversight board of the Tila ejido from 2018 to 2021 and was a leading defender in the struggle for restitution of the ejido's territory against dispossession. She was also a member of the National Indigenous Congress (CNI).

name: Samantha Carolina Gomes Fonseca
summary: Samantha Carolina Gomes Fonseca was shot dead in a premeditated attack as she left a visit to the South Men's Preventive Prison in Mexico City on 14 January 2024. She was a politician and an activist for the rights of trans people and incarcerated people in Mexico City. In 2022, she received the Medal of Merit for Human Rights Defenders from the Congress of Mexico City.

name: Angélica Meraz León
summary: Angélica Meraz León was shot and killed at her place of business on 9 February 2024. She was president of Unión y Fuerza por Nuestros Desaparecidos in Baja California, advocating for families with disappeared loved ones after her brother was disappeared in 2018.

name: Javier Ochoa Tejeda
summary: Javier Ochoa Tejeda was kidnapped by ten men on 13 February 2024; his dead body was found hours later in the local sports field. He led the environmental defence against a sanitary landfill at Paso de Ovejas, Veracruz, alongside other residents of the village of Palmaritos, and also opposed the construction of a poultry farm in Tierra Colorada. Ochoa argued that both projects would cause environmental harm and health hazards for the surrounding communities. He and other residents of Palmaritos had received death threats over their environmental work, and several attacks connected to the landfill project have been documented.

name: Noé Sandoval Adame
summary: Noé Sandoval Adame was shot dead in Zumpango, near Chilpancingo, Guerrero on 13 February 2024. He was a member of the María Herrera Chilpancingo Collective and an advocate for families of the disappeared, after his son was disappeared in 2023.

name: Florentino Castro
summary: Florentino Castro was killed on the lower slopes of the Iztaccíhuatl volcano on 25 February 2024, while he and two fellow rangers — José Ángel Pelcastre and Ventura Ojeda  — were digging a ditch to block the vehicles the loggers used, He was a forest ranger and a member of the San Andrés Hueyacatitla ejido in San Salvador el Verde, Puebla.

name: José Ángel Pelcastre
summary: José Ángel Pelcastre was killed on the lower slopes of the Iztaccíhuatl volcano on 25 February 2024, while he and two fellow rangers — Ventura Ojeda and Florentino Castro — were digging a ditch to block the vehicles the loggers used. He was a forest ranger and a member of the San Andrés Hueyacatitla ejido in San Salvador el Verde, Puebla.

name: Ventura Ojeda
summary: Ventura Ojeda was killed on the lower slopes of the Iztaccíhuatl volcano on 25 February 2024, while he and two fellow rangers — José Ángel Pelcastre and Florentino Castro — were digging a ditch to block the vehicles the loggers used. He was a forest ranger and a member of the San Andrés Hueyacatitla ejido in San Salvador el Verde, Puebla.

name: Palemón Vásquez Cajero
summary: Palemón Vásquez Cajero was shot by a person on a motorcycle as he returned home in Santiago Jamiltepec, Oaxaca on 18 March 2024. A Mixtec teacher and promoter of Indigenous education, he was a member of Section 22 of the CNTE teachers' union and secretary of his community's ejido commission.

name: Antonio Regis Nicolas
summary: Antonio Regis Nicolás was shote dead while walking home on the evening of 7 May 2024 with his wife and two-year-old son after taking the child for emergency medical care. The family was accosted by armed men in military fatigues, who separated Nicolás from his family and, on confirming that he was a resident of Santa María Ostula, murdered him. A Nahua Indigenous leader and human rights defender, Nicolás worked to protect Santa María Ostula—23 communities in the coastal and mountain region of Michoacán—and its territory against dispossession and the exploitation of natural resources by organised crime groups; the community has endured threats, intimidation, homicides and disappearances in defending its autonomy and self-determination.

name: Ignacio Lopez
beat: Family killed: ; Arturo Lopez Gomez; Florentino Lopez;Alonzo Lopez; Berenice de Jesus Almazán Gonzalez; Rosaly Valen; Dolores Almazán Saldovar; and other unidentified persons
summary: Ignacio López and ten members of his family were murdered in their home on the afternoon of 12 May 2024. Following the murders, the attackers burned the victims' bodies. López was a member of the Nuevo Morelia ejido in Chicomsuelo, Chiapas known for his outspoken opposition to the violent practices of criminal groups in the area. He and his family had resisted pressure to cooperate with organised crime and continued to protect their land from illegal mining.

name: Alberto Cortina Vasquez
summary: Alberto Cortina Vásquez and his brother Jorge Cortina Vázquez were murdered by members of the Veracruz state police on 20 June 2024 in Perote, Veracruz. Both were defenders of water and took part in the Movement in Defence of Water in the Libres–Oriental Basin, which had been protesting against the appropriation of water, the use of hail cannons and pollution from several hog farms; the state government responded to the protests by sending law enforcement officers who pursued people into their homes, fired guns, beat protesters and made arbitrary arrests.

name: Jorge Cortina Vázquez
summary: Jorge Cortina Vázquez and his brother Alberto Cortina Vásquez were murdered by members of the Veracruz state police on 20 June 2024 in Perote, Veracruz. Both were defenders of water and took part in the Movement in Defence of Water in the Libres–Oriental Basin, which had been protesting against the appropriation of water, the use of hail cannons and pollution from several hog farms; the state government responded to the protests by sending law enforcement officers who pursued people into their homes, fired guns, beat protesters and made arbitrary arrests.

name: Minerva Pérez Castro
summary: Minerva Pérez Castro was attacked by three armed men and killed on 8 July 2024 as she left her place of business in her car. A businesswoman and president of the National Fishing Industry Chamber in Baja California, she operated in full compliance with environmental rules, promoted sustainable fishing and publicly reported illegal fishing in a region where the authorities had failed to address it—work that made her the target of repeated threats and extortion.

name: Alberto Berales
summary: Alberto Berales was shot dead on 18 July 2024 in the municipality of Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero, together with his godmother María de Jesús Pasado. He was a promoter of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ) from the community of Buenavista.

name: Lorenzo Santos Torres
summary: Lorenzo Santos Torres was murdered on the road between San Martín Lachila and San Andrés Zabache, Oaxaca, together with his wife and daughter on 18 July 2024. They were shot and their car was burned with their bodies inside. Torres was a Mixtec man who had been imprisoned for opposing the regional chieftainship of Santiago Amoltepec.

name: María de Jesús Pasado
summary: María de Jesús Pasado was shot dead on 18 July 2024 in the municipality of Chilapa de Álvarez, Guerrero, together with her godson Alberto Berales. She was a member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ) from the community of Alcozacán.

name: Leunim Gómez Girón
summary: Leumim Gómez Girón was shot by armed men on a motorcycle outside his home in San Cristóbal de las Casas, Chiapas, on 22 July 2024. A lawyer from Ocosingo and a former state prosecution officer, he was the legal adviser to the Tianguis Campesino of Ocosingo—the peasant producers' market organisation—in its dispute with the COMACH vendor association that had seized the market's premises; he had received death threats from COMACH members.

name: Rafael González López
summary: Rafael González López was shot dead on the morning of 25 July 2024 as he walked along one of the main streets in the centre of Santiago Juxtlahuaca, Oaxaca. A Triqui leader of the Movimiento de Unificación y Lucha Triqui Independiente (MULTI), he worked as a human rights defender on behalf of local merchants.

name: Vicente Ramírez Santiago
summary: Vicente Ramírez Santiago was found dead in Juchitán, Oaxaca, with signs of torture and gunshot wounds on 30 July 2024. Known as “Rosty Bazendú," he was a Binnizá (Zapotec) rapper and a defender of the diidxazá language and Zapotec culture.

name: Antonio Carrillo
summary: Antonio Carrillo and Yuniur Vázquez Rosalío were last seen on 10 August 2024 in Colotlán, Jalisco; they were found dead in an overturned pickup truck down a ravine. A Wixárika activist in Bolaños, Carrillo was campaign coordinator to Vázquez, the Wixárika mayor-elect of Bolaños.

name: Yuniur Vázquez Rosalío
summary: Yuniur Vázquez Rosalío and Antonio Carrillo were last seen on 10 August 2024 in Colotlán, Jalisco; they were found dead in an overturned pickup truck down a ravine. A Wixárika activist, Vázquez was the mayor-elect of Bolaños for the local party Hagamos.

name: Daniel Bautista Vásquez
summary: Daniel Bautista Vásquez was was found dead after being missing for nine days on 14 September 2024. A Mixtec man from Tlaxiaco, Oaxaca, he had been under precautionary protecgtion measures from the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights since 18 July after reporting that municipal police had tortured his brother.

name: Jordan Terjiño Luna
summary: Jordán Terjiño Luna was killed when about ten gunmen with high-calibre rifles ambushed the vehicle he was travelling in Olinalá, Guerrero on 8 March 2021. He was a Nahua member of the Indigenous and Popular Council of Guerrero – Emiliano Zapata (CIPOG-EZ), which campaigns for territorial rights, autonomy and self-determination.

name: Jesus Alejandro Marquez Jimenez
outlet: Published the weekly Orión Informativo, worked for media outlet Crítica Digital Noticias for 8 years
beat: Crime reporter
summary: Jesús Alejandro Márquez Jiménez left a family gathering on his motorcycle after taking a phone call and was found the next day lying face down with three bullet wounds beside a road near the Amado Nervo airport in Tepic, Nayarit; relatives identified the body on 2 December. He was the first journalist killed in the López Obrador administration, on its opening day. Nayarit state officials were later arrested over the killing.

name: Diego García Corona
outlet: Weekly Morelos outlet #Edomex ('Semanario de Morelos')
beat: General news
summary: Diego García Corona was shot dead by a group of armed men on a motorcycle while driving his car in Ecatepec, State of Mexico; his press credentials were found on his body. García Corona was a reporter for the weekly Semanario Morelos in Ecatepec.

name: Rafael Murúa Manríquez
outlet: Radiokashana FM (Director of Radio Station)
beat: Organization of the American States (OAS) wrote that he addressed cultural and political topics, and was also a human rights defender and activist. Murúa denounced harassment and threats after writing comments that were critical of the administration of Mulegé Mayor Felipe Prado Bautista.
summary: Rafael Murúa Manríquez was abducted on the night of 19 January 2019 and his body was found the following day beside the highway north of Santa Rosalía, Baja California Sur. Murúa was the director of Radiokashana FM, a community radio station in Santa Rosalía, and had been under the federal protection mechanism since 2017 after receiving threats.

name: Jesús Ramos Rodríguez
outlet: Nuestra Región Hoy on XHEMZ-FM
beat: Hosted a very popular morning show called Nuestra Región HOY. It had become increasingly controversial in the wake of recent municipal elections, according to the journalist’s brother (CPJ). He appears to have criticized local politicians.
summary: Jesús Eugenio Ramos Rodríguez was shot by a lone gunman at about 7 a.m. while having breakfast in a hotel restaurant in Emiliano Zapata, Tabasco, and died of his wounds in hospital that morning. Ramos presented the news programme “Nuestra Región Hoy” on Radio Oye 99.9 FM, where he had worked for nearly 20 years.

name: Reynaldo López
outlet: Motores del Desierto
beat: Sports
summary: Reynaldo López was killed at about 5:50 p.m. when gunmen in another car fired at least 14 times into the vehicle he was travelling in on a main street in the Las Pilas neighbourhood of Hermosillo, Sonora; his colleague Carlos Cota Rubio was wounded and survived. López was a radio announcer who had worked for several stations in Hermosillo.

name: Samir Flores Soberanes
outlet: Producer at Amiltzinko Community Radio, member of The Peoples in Defense of Land and Water Front, Indigenous activist
beat: Environmental defender, activist
summary: Samir Flores Soberanes was gunned down on the doorstep of his home in Amilcingo, Morelos. Flores was a co-founder of the community radio station Radio Comunitaria Amiltzinko and a leading opponent of the Proyecto Integral Morelos gas pipeline and thermoelectric plants. He was killed days after challenging government representatives about the project at a public meeting and just before a referendum was to decide its future.

name: Omar Iván Camacho
outlet: Broadcaster at a news program called Altavoz, ran the website Évora Sport
beat: Sports
summary: Omar Iván Camacho disappeared after covering a morning baseball game and was found that evening under a bridge on a dirt road leading to La Escalera, Sinaloa. His body showed signs of torture, blows and marks left by handcuffs, and he died of closed head trauma caused by blunt force. The men held as his presumed killers were later released.

name: Santiago Barroso
outlet: Journalist and university professor, hosted the daily radio news program “Buenos Días San Luis”
beat: General news. IFJ reported that Barroso had denounced the presence of individuals linked to human trafficking and drug trafficking in Sonora the day before he was killed.
summary: Santiago Barroso Alfaro was shot three times when he opened the door of his home in the Sonora neighbourhood of San Luis Río Colorado, Sonora. Barroso hosted the morning news programme “Buenos Días San Luis” on Río Digital 91.1 FM, founded and edited the news website Red 653 and wrote for the weekly Semanario Contraseña.

name: Telésforo Santiago Enriquez
outlet: El Cafetal (98.7 FM),  a community radio station based in the town of San Agustin Loxicha and member of local teacher's union
beat: Mostly Indigenous language/cultural preservation. The day before he was killed, he took radio calls from listeners on the topic of local politicans and embezzlement.
summary: Telésforo Santiago Enríquez was ambushed and shot dead in his vehicle in the Ampliación de las Tres Cruces neighbourhood of San Agustín Loxicha, Oaxaca, as he drove to his station. Santiago Enríquez was a retired teacher who founded and directed the community radio station El Cafetal.

name: Francisco Romero Díaz
outlet: Founded Facebook media outlet Ocurrió Aquí
beat: Crime
summary: Francisco Romero Díaz, known as “Ñaca-Ñaca," was shot dead by unidentified gunmen in the early hours in the car park of a bar in Playa del Carmen, Quintana Roo, three blocks from the Solidaridad state police base. Romero covered crime and local politics for the newspaper Quintana Roo Hoy and ran the Facebook news page “Ocurrió Aquí." He was under the federal protection at the time of his murder, having been assigned bodyguards after two colleagues at Semanario Playa News were killed.

name: Norma Sarabia
outlet: Tabasco Hoy
beat: Police and security. The week before the attack, Tabasco Hoy published a report dated in Huimanguillo, without any author credit, in which Mayor José del Carmen Torruco is accused of covering up corruption and nepotism in the Municipal Police Directorate.
summary: Norma Sarabia Garduza was shot by two armed men as she entered her home in the Club Liberal neighbourhood of Huimanguillo, Tabasco. Sarabia was a correspondent in Huimanguillo for the newspapers Tabasco Hoy and Diario Presente, covering crime and security, and had worked as a journalist for more than 20 years.

name: Juan Escamilla Bautista
summary: Juan Escamilla Bautista, head of the printing facilities for the Expreso newspaper in Ciudad Victoria, was shot at a small mechanic's workshop he kept in the La Presita neighbourhood. The Expreso de Victoria was previously targeted by organized crime including the detonation of an IED in 2012, and in 2018, a head was left in a cooler in front of the offices.

name: Rogelio Barragán
outlet: Founder of Guerrero Al Instante
beat: Courts and crime
summary: Rogelio Barragán Pérez's body was found inside the boot of his car in the Benito Juárez neighbourhood of Zacatepec, Morelos. Barragán was the director of the news website Guerrero al Instante, for which he also reported on crime.

name: Jorge Celestino Ruíz Váquez
outlet: El Gráfico de Xalapa
beat: Covered general news, including local politics, crime, and violence. Days before his murder, he published an article in which he pointed out an alleged embezzlement of “between 10 and 12 million pesos” by José Paulino Domínguez Sánchez, municipal president of Actopan, Veracruz, who was later alleged by the killer to have ordered the attack.
summary: Jorge Celestino Ruíz Váquez was attacked and killed with a firearm around 9:15 pm in the town of La Bocanita in the Actopan region of Veracuz. Ruíz Váquez was the reporter for the newspaper El Gráfico in Veracruz.

name: Edgar Alberto Nava López
outlet: Founder of La Verdad Zihuatenejo. Formerly a reporter for El Diario de Zihuatanejo and El Despertar de la Costa
beat: Local government, crime, violence
summary: Edgar Alberto Nava López was shot at about 10 a.m. while on the beach taking a tour with a group of children as part of an activity organized by the City Council in Zihuatanejo, Guerrero. Nava founded and directed the news website La Verdad de Zihuatanejo, where he covered crime, and also served as director of regulations for the Zihuatanejo municipal government.

name: Nevith Condés Jaramillo
outlet: Founder of El Observatorio del Sur. Previously radio show host for local station Radio Roca.
beat: General news
summary: Nevith Condés Jaramillo was found dead with multiple stab wounds at Cerro de Cacalotepec, in Tejupilco, State of Mexico. Condés was the director of the news portal El Observatorio del Sur, which covered citizen complaints and local affairs in the south of the state.

name: Erick Castillo Sánchez
outlet: Filmmaker and documentarian, contracted with Discovery Channel and National Geographic
beat: As an independent filmmaker, he worked on a number of themes, though none of them stand out as paricularly subversive aside from a 2013 documentary collaboration on human trafficking. He had recently collaborated on the film Roma with director Alfonso Cuarón in Mexico City.
summary: Erick Castillo Sánchez was shot dead by armed men who confronted him and his wife at a convenience store on the Barra Vieja highway in Acapulco, Guerrero, and ordered the couple out of their car and into a van. His wife, the photographer Estefanía Carpio, ran and hid in a shed. Castillo was a cinematographer who worked with Discovery Channel in Latin America and had contributed to the Oscar-winning film Roma.

name: Álvaro Ruiz
outlet: Manager of Radio Pichucalco 102.1 FM
beat: General news and event coverage. Ruiz was also responsible for administrative tasks at the radio station.
summary: Álvaro Ruiz was found dead at his home in Pichucalco, Chiapas. The outlet Reversos reported that his body bore a head injury and at least two stab wounds to the left side of the chest; no other reporting gives any account of the circumstances of his death. Ruiz was a radio announcer and station manager.

name: Fidel Ávila Gómez
outlet: Radio announcer and manager at the "La Ke Buena" radio station
beat: A relative told CPJ that Ávila had worked there for 20 years, managing the station's finances and regularly presenting newscasts.
summary: Fidel Ávila Gómez was last seen on 29 November 2019 and reported missing three weeks later; his body, shot, was recovered on 8 January 2020 by soldiers patrolling Michoacán's Tierra Caliente region. Accounts differ over whether he was found decomposing inside his own car beside the San Lucas–Huetamo highway or in a ditch. Ávila was an announcer and manager at the radio station La Ke Buena.

name: Teresa Aracely Alcocer
outlet: Radio announcer for La Poderosa
beat:
In her last social media posts on Facebook, Alcocer wrote: “Children are not to be beaten; they are not to be abused, and they are not to be killed,” and she condemned the murder of Fatima, a girl in Mexico City.

Alcocer's regular radio segment concerned taarot readings, horoscopes, and palm readings. Bárbara Greco was her radio name.
summary: Teresa Aracely Alcocer was shot twice in the head while standing in the street talking with her father outside her home in the El Barrial neighbourhood of Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua; other accounts place the shooting as she was getting out of a pickup truck. Alcocer was a radio announcer who broadcast under the name Bárbara Greco.

name: Gitler Oseguera Barrera
outlet: Worked at several radio stations including La Zeta and La Tremenda
beat: Recorded commercials, public address announcements
summary: Gitler Oseguera Barrera was shot in the head as he got into his car after finishing work as an entertainer at Free Bar in Morelia, Michoacán. No motive has been established. Oseguera was a radio announcer known on air as El Tazito.

name: María Elena Ferral
outlet: Correspondent for the regional newspapers Diario de Xalapa and El Heraldo de Poza Rica. Founder of the Quinto Poder de Veracruz
beat: Ferral often covered kidnappings and enforced disappearances, some of which were blamed on the local police.
summary: María Elena Ferral was shot at least three times by masked men on a motorcycle at about 2 p.m. in a street in Papantla, Veracruz, and died in hospital a few hours later. Ferral was a correspondent for the newspaper El Diario de Xalapa and a co-founder of the local news website El Quinto Poder.

name: Víctor Fernando Álvarez Chávez
outlet: News editor for news website Punto x Punto Noticias
beat: General and political news
summary: Víctor Fernando Álvarez Chávez disappeared on 2 April 2020 in Guerrero. His severed head was found near a secondary school six days later, and DNA testing confirmed his identity on 11 April. Reporters Without Borders described the killing as execution-style.

name: Jorge Miguel Armenta Ávalos
outlet: Owner of Medios Obson, newspaper "El Tiempo"
beat: Business, Corruption, Crime, Politics, Sports
summary: Jorge Miguel Armenta Ávalos was shot by armed men as he left a restaurant in the centre of Ciudad Obregón, Sonora, in an attack that also killed one of the officers with him. Armenta was the founder and owner of Medios Obson, publisher of the daily El Tiempo and the weekly Última Palabra, and had been enrolled in federal protection since 2016 after threats against the outlet's staff.

name: Pablo Morrugares Parraguirre
outlet: Director of PM Noticias
beat: Crime, security, politics. Prior to the murder, the website had published stories about violence in the state, political events, and the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on Guerrero (CPJ).
summary: Pablo Morrugares Parraguirre and the police officer assigned to protect him were shot 53 times shortly before 1 a.m. in a restaurant in Iguala, Guerrero. Morrugares was the founder and editor of the news website PM Noticias, which covered crime and policing in central Guerrero, and had been under federal protection since surviving an attack in 2016.

name: Juan Nelcio Espinoza Menera
outlet: Valedor TV
beat: Spot news, crime, local events, general news
summary: Juan Nelcio Espinoza Menera died in police custody after being detained by Coahuila state Fuerza Única officers while covering violence in Piedras Negras on the night of 20 August 2020. His body showed signs of torture, with fractures to his arms and spine, strangulation and head injuries. Espinoza was an independent reporter who created and ran the digital outlet El Valedor TV.

name: Julio Valdivia
outlet: Reporter for El Mundo de Córdoba
beat: Covered mainly current events, specializing in crime, accidents, and natural disasters. Valdivia's last report was published on September 7, covering a shootout in Cosolapa, a town in Oaxaca separated by one street from Tezonapa, Veracruz, and where the Jalisco Nueva Generación Cartel operates. Two days later, he was killed.
summary: Julio Valdivia Rodríguez's mutilated and decapitated body was found on the railway tracks near Motzorongo, in Tezonapa, Veracruz, beside his motorcycle. Valdivia was the regional correspondent in Tezonapa for the newspaper El Mundo de Córdoba, where he had worked since 2014 covering crime and security.

name: Arturo Alba Medina
outlet: Host of Telediarios, a nightly news program on Channel 6
beat: Medina was a newscaster who covered a broad range of topics. According to La Verdad, he had recently covered the death of a young woman at the hands of police in Chihuahua, clashes between suspected gang members and police, and allegations of police corruption.
summary: Arturo Alba Medina left the news station after his nightly broadcast at about 10 p.m. and was shot eleven times by two armed men in a moving vehicle as he sat in his car in Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua; reports differ over whether he was parked or already driving. Alba presented the nightly news; his killers were later convicted and sentenced.

name: Victor Manuel Jimenez Campos
outlet: Reporter for Rotativa Digital de Guanajuato, Nota Roja Celaya, Digital Noticias
beat: Crime and security
summary: Víctor Manuel Jiménez Campos was last seen covering a baseball game in the community of Elguera, Guanajuato, on 1 November 2020, and was reported missing three days later. Friends and family searching the surrounding farmland found only his bloodstained T-shirt and one sneaker. His remains were recovered on 10 June 2024 from an abandoned water well in Torrecillas, Villagrán, nearly four years after he vanished.

name: Jesús Alfonso Piñuelas
outlet: Founder of Zarathustra Press and El Shock de la Noticia
beat: Reported on crime and security in Cajeme, including the murder of a municipal police officer for Zarathustra Press.
summary: Jesús Alfonso Piñuelas was shot dead while riding his motorcycle in Sonora. One man was later sentenced for the killing.

name: Israel Vázquez Rangel
outlet: Reporter for El Salmantino
beat: Crime and security were his specialty. On November 2, he wrote a piece about bodies in plastic bags found throughout Salamanca, allegedly planted by organized crime groups, and on November 6 he uploaded a video about recent murders in the city.
summary: Israel Vázquez Rangel reached the scene of a reported body dump in Salamanca, Guanajuato, ahead of the police and was preparing to go live on Facebook when men in a vehicle drew up and shot him at least five times; he died of his wounds in hospital shortly afterwards. Vázquez was a reporter for El Salmantino, and the third Mexican journalist killed in two weeks. His murderer was later sentenced to 27 and a half years.

name: Jaime Daniel Castaño Zacarías
outlet: Photojournalist for Jerez City Hall, Owner of prensalibremx.com
beat: General news photographer, but didn't usually cover violence. On his website, he primarily focused on political and social information, mostly supporting the local government. Also covered environmental issues.
summary: Jaime Daniel Castaño Zacarías stopped to photograph two bound bodies with gunshot wounds and a narco-message left in a street in Jerez, Zacatecas, at about 10 a.m., before the authorities had arrived. Someone at the scene told him to delete the images and he refused. He was later forced off the road while riding his motorcycle and shot dead; local reports say the men also took the memory card from his camera. Castaño was a photojournalist.

name: Benjamín Morales Hernández
outlet: Reporter for Noticias Xonoidag
beat: Police, politics, local news. The day before he was kidnapped, he posted a video on his media outlet on Facebook describing the upcomping June elections, and shared that he was receiving anonymous threats.
summary: Benjamín Morales Hernández was taken from his home by armed men on the night of 2 May 2021; the next day his body, shot several times, was found beside the Sonoyta–Caborca highway in Sonora with a narco-message. Morales founded and ran Noticias Xonoidag, a Facebook-based news outlet covering local affairs and politics in Sonoyta.

name: Gustavo Sánchez Cabrera
outlet: Editor of La Policiaca, and his own page Noticias Minuto a Minuto
beat: Crime, courts, local politics
summary: Gustavo Sánchez Cabrera was shot twice, once fatally in the head, by two gunmen at about 8:30 a.m. as he rode a motorcycle with his son on the road between San Vicente and Morro Mazatán, in Santo Domingo Tehuantepec, Oaxaca. Sánchez edited the news portal La Policiaca del Istmo in Salina Cruz and covered crime and politics in the Isthmus of Tehuantepec for the Facebook-based outlet Panorama Pacífico; he had survived an attempt on his life in July 2020. He attempted to incorperate into the federal Protection Mechanism for years after having protection revoked in 2014, and although he had been accepted into the program at the time of his death, none of the protective measures were in place.

name: Enrique García García
outlet: Reports claim that worked for several media outlets including Radio y Televisión Mexiquense and El Sol de Toluca. He and in the state's communications offices for state government, the Ministry of Security, and in the City Council of Tenango del Valle
beat: Ana Muñiz Neyra, the incoming mayor of San Mateo Atenco, attended García's wake. He had handled media relations for her during the last election campaign. As a result, García was expected to join the municipal council of San Mateo Atenco by December 2021.
summary: Enrique García García was found shot dead in his car in Metepec, State of Mexico, a day after his family last heard from him. According to the state prosecutor's account, three people asked him for a ride that night; at a certain point the woman got out of the car and ordered her companions to shoot the driver. Those charged with his murder were later released.

name: Saúl Tijerina Rentería
outlet: Freelanced for La Policiaca and Noticias en la Web, both Facebook-based outlets
beat: Provided drone footage of news events and occasionally standard camera photography for both news outlets. According to CPJ, he had been working for La Policiaca for six months and Noticias for ten months, when he was killed. General assignment reporter, often covering sports, crime, and security.
summary: Saúl Tijerina Rentería was stabbed several times in the neck after leaving work at 2:40 a.m. and was found hours later at the junction of the Libramiento Surponiente and the Antiguo Camino in Coahuila; accounts differ over whether he lay beside his car or in its trunk. Article 19 reported that a sign was left with his body reading “This is what will happen to all the snitches in the state or those who collaborate with the state, CDN."

name: Abraham Mendoza Mendoza
outlet: Host, news director, and producer of the show VocesRadio. He also reported for EXA-Morelia, another local radio station, and hosted programmes on Central TV AM, and Grupo Acir radio, and Vasco de Quiroga University’s Observatorio program (his alma mater).
beat: On social media, he was often outspoken in his criticism of political corruption, both local and federal.
summary: Abraham Mendoza Mendoza was getting into his car in the car park of a gym in the Nueva Valladolid neighbourhood of Morelia, Michoacán, when a man walked up and shot him; a second man sat in the passenger seat of the car keeping watch. Two men were later found guilty of his murder.

name: Ricardo Domínguez López
outlet: Founder and editor of InfoGuaymas portal, Reporter for Televisa Sonora
beat: Broad range of topics including municipal, state, national, and international news, as well as crime and security. CPJ stated that most website articles were unattributed to a single author. In March, he covered a deadly shootout in Guaymas.
summary: Ricardo Domínguez López was shot with a .38 calibre handgun at about 5:30 p.m. in a shop car park opposite the municipal police headquarters in Guaymas, Sonora, on his 47th birthday. Domínguez founded and edited the news website InfoGuaymas and was president of the Asociación Metropolitana de Periodistas Independientes de Guaymas-Empalme.

name: Jacinto Romero Flores
outlet: Anchored radio show “Dígalo Sin Miedo” on the station Ori Stereo; hosted Facebook show “El Enano del Tapanco;" wrote a blog called Tiempo Extra
beat: Corruption, crime, and politics. It was reported that at the time of his death, there was a pending investigation into a complaint filed against Flores by Crispín Hernández, president of the Municipal Council of Mixtla de Altamirano. Hernández accused Flores of attempted extortion and moral damages for publishing articles against him that spoke of alleged nepotism and supposed mismanagement by public servants in that municipality.
summary: Jacinto Romero Flores was shot several times in his vehicle while driving to work in Veracruz. The car was clearly marked “prensa,”the Spanish word for press. He had reported receiving threats over WhatsApp before he was killed.

name: Manuel González Reyes
outlet: Founder and director of Portal Morelos Noticias
beat:
Local news, especially business, politics and crime. He had recently been covering local murders and shooting attacks.

Reyes had been covering a landslide in Jiutepec the morning he was killed and had denounced the political inaction regarding a response. “There’s no support from the state and federal representatives, the senators, the governor, or the other mayors who also live off our taxes,” he said in a Facebook Live broadcast by Portal Morelos.
summary: Jesús Manuel González Reyes was shot in the head by two armed men on a motorcycle after having lunch in the Miraval neighbourhood of Cuernavaca, Morelos. González, 55, founded and ran the Facebook-based news outlet Portal Morelos Noticias.

name: Freddy López Arévalo
outlet: News anchor at the station XERA-Radio Uno; ran the magazine "Jovel"
beat: General news reporting including the impact of armed groups, but crime was not his focus. He did a lot of international / national / local news roundups. A few hours before his death, he made a final post on social media, highlighting the case of 200 workers who were laid off from the city council of San Cristóbal de las Casas, Chiapas.
summary: Freddy López Arévalo was shot dead outside his home in San Cristóbal de las Casas, Chiapas, in front of his family; the gunman left by motorcycle. The two men suspected of killing him were themselves later found dead, and four years on his family was still demanding justice.

name: Alfredo Cardoso Echeverría
outlet: Founder and editor of Las Dos Costas Periodismo Plural, also listed as a photojournalist in some reports
beat: Unclear exactly what Cardoso reported on, but it was determined that he was killed due to his journalistic work. He was also widely reported to be a photojournalist as well as author of the Facebook page where he reported.
summary: Alfredo Cardoso Echeverría was seized from his home at night by masked, armed men and found the next morning with multiple gunshot wounds near the house, by some accounts in his own driveway. He died in the hospital in Acapulco, Guerrero. One man has since been convicted of the murder.

name: José Luis Arenas Gamboa
outlet: Founder and editor of Inforegio, Founder and editor of La Noticia
beat: Politics, corruption. Infobae reported that Gamboa Arenas had recently posted a severe critique of the level of insecurity and protection afforded by municipal authorities in the port of Veracruz, allowing the apparent extortion of protection money in neighborhoods of the city, identifying by name the criminal groups responsible for it, on social media. Article 19 reported that two of Gamboa's most recent publications, ‘La Guerra por la Narco Política’ [‘The War for Narco Politics’] and ‘Prospectiva parte 1’ [‘Prospective part 1’], documented violence in the region and criticised the failure to combat it. He was known for his live broadcasts in which he often criticized the wave of violence in Veracruz and the extortion of businesses in the city.
summary: José Luis Gamboa Arenas was found with multiple stab wounds in the Floresta neighbourhood of the port of Veracruz; accounts differ over whether he died at the scene or in hospital three days later. Four days passed before he was identified.

name: Margarito Martinez
outlet: Freelance photojournalist
beat: Specialized in crime scene photography
summary: Alfonso Margarito Martínez Esquivel was ambushed and shot dead outside his home in Tijuana, Baja California. He had returned briefly after finishing an assignment and was about to go out again to photograph in another part of the city. Martínez was a crime photojournalist; a man accused of relaying the order to kill him was later sent for trial.

name: Lourdes Maldonado López
outlet: Broadcast reporter for Sintoniza Sin Censura, radio host of Brebaje
beat:
General news, corruption, and local politics. In her most recent broadcasts on Brebaje, she covered a wide range of topics, including criticism of the creation of a magazine by the Tijuana municipal government, as well as the murder of her colleague Margarito Martínez.

Days before her murder, she won her lawsuit against Jamie Bonilla.
summary: Lourdes Maldonado López was shot dead inside her car as she arrived at her home in the Santa Fe neighbourhood of Tijuana, Baja California. Attackers waited until her escort had left. Maldonado covered politics and corruption in Baja California for three decades, working for Televisa, Primer Sistema de Noticias (PSN) and the weekly Séptimo Día, and in her last months presenting the programme “Brebaje” on the radio station Sintoniza sin Fronteras. In 2019 she had told President López Obrador at his morning press conference that she feared for her life. Maldonado was enrolled in protective measures at the time of her death.

name: Roberto Toledo
outlet: Monitor Michoacan, Camera operator, photographer, and video editor
beat:
General news coverage, mostly as a photographer and camera operator. Toledo published an article in November 2020, “Cheap Works or Crony Deals?” in which he pointed out the alleged corruption in public works projects funded by the municipal government. Last story he was working on involved the alleged illicit enrichment of authorities at the Zitácuaro Senior Citizens' Home. The Monitor's reporting was the only news source in the city that investigated city hall.

January 27, four days before the attack, Monitor Michoacan published a short commentary criticizing state authorities for allegedly changing information about people arrested on drug possession (non-attributed, more likely to have been authored by Armando Linares).
summary: Roberto Toledo was shot in the carport of the headquarters of Monitor Michoacán, in Zitácuaro, Michoacán. Returning from a corner shop with sodas, he was approached by two men who asked “where the lawyer was,” referring to the lawfirm that also worked in the offices, and followed him into a courtyard and executed him off camera. Minutes later one of them came back to throw down two pieces of cardboard, one signed by the CJNG reading: “This is what will happen to all the lawyers who handle cases for La Familia Michoacana.”

name: Heber López Vázquez
outlet: Founder and editor of NoticiasWeb and RCP Noticias
beat: General assignment, but was covering political issues and a large project related to the federal megaproject Interoceanic Corridor of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec when he was killed. According to El Pais, the day before he was killed, Heber had published a report accusing local politician Arminda Espinosa Cartas of corruption and mismanagement in the construction of the breakwater in Salinas del Marqués, Oaxaca (part of the Interoceanic Corridor of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec) — specifically accusing her of coercing construction workers to vote for her in upcoming elections, or be fired. Arminda's brother was convicted as one of the killers.
summary: Heber López Vázquez was shot dead in the radio studio he ran out of his own home in Salina Cruz, Oaxaca, by one of two men who arrived in a pickup truck. His 12-year-old son hid until the gunmen had left.

name: Jorge Luis Camero Zazueta
outlet: Director and reporter for El Informativo
beat: General news. In September 2021 he assumed the position of private secretary to Mayor Luis Fuentes Aguilar. Two weeks before he was murdered, he had requested a leave of absence from that position to return to journalism, due to accusations that he was involved in the kidnapping and murder of former congressman Daniel Palafox Suárez.
summary: Jorge Luis Camero Zazueta was shot eight times while working out at a local gym in Sonora. Officials claimed his murder was unrelated to his work, a characterization noted by civil society organizations that relates to a pattern of authorities rapidly dismissing journalistic motives in the killing of reporters.

name: Juan Carlos Muñiz
outlet: Crime reporter for Testigo Minero
beat: Covered organized crime, using the pseudonyms “Rigoberto” and “El TX" for bylines. CPJ also reported the pseudonym "Testigo Minero" was used for a lot of political reporting (same name as the outlet), but couldn't confirm if it was linked to Muñiz.
summary: Juan Carlos Muñiz was found shot dead in the Los Olivos neighbourhood in Zacatecas, in the car he used both to reach assignments and to earn a living as a taxi driver.

name: Armando Linares López
outlet: Founder and investigative reporter for Monitor Michoacán
beat:
According to the NYT, Linares founded Monitor Michoacán on the premise that if Mexico hoped to escape the violence that was consuming it, the press had to go after the politicians who enabled and facilitated crime. Linares reported on contract fraud, bribery, and police extortion. The Monitor's reporting was the only news source in the city that investigated city hall. The Monitor was financed by a local lawyer, and ran out of the law office.

In 2021, year before his murder, Monitor Michoacán big story was the mayor, Juan Antonio Ixtláhuac Orihuela, who 12 years earlier had been arrested by federal agents after his name appeared on CJNG's payroll. Case fell apart and Orihuela remained in politics, and had regained his role as mayor.
summary: Armando Linares López was found dead in his flat, shot eight times, 43 days after the murder of his colleague Roberto Toledo. Surveillance footage showed two lookouts in place hours before the killing, and the man later accused of the murder was released. Linares was founder and news director of Monitor Michoacán. Reports vary on whether he was enrolled in the federal Protection Mechanism.

name: Luis Enrique Ramírez Ramos
outlet: Director of Fuentes Fidedignas, columnist for El Debate
beat: Local political issues
summary: Luis Enrique Ramírez Ramos left his home in the Los Pinos neighbourhood of Culiacán, Sinaloa, at about 3 a.m. and was abducted close by. His body was found wrapped in black plastic sheeting on a dirt road in the municipality. An autopsy determined he had died of a brain injury caused by blows to the head. The killing remained unpunished.

name: Yessenia Mollinedo Falconi
outlet: Director of El Veraz News
beat: Mollinedo previously covered crime and security for El Veraz but stopped doing so after receiving numerous death threats over the past few years, according to the journalist’s brother, Ramiro Mollinedo Falconi, who spoke with CPJ. Most of her articles had been taken down out of concern for her safety.
summary: Yessenia Mollinedo Falconi and her camera operator Sheila Johana García Olivera were shot at about 4 p.m. by gunmen lying in wait outside a convenience store in Cosoleacaque, Veracruz; both were taken to hospital and died of their injuries. Mollinedo was the founder and director of the digital outlet El Veraz, which covers southern Veracruz.

name: Sheila Johana García
outlet: Camera operator for El Veraz News
beat: Recently-hired camera operator. Her death is likely collatoral damage by proximity to Molliendo, who seemed to be the target.
summary: Sheila Johana García Olivera and the reporter Yessenia Mollinedo Falconi were shot at about 4 p.m. by gunmen lying in wait outside a convenience store in Cosoleacaque, Veracruz; both were taken to hospital and died of their injuries. García had recently been hired as a camera operator at the digital outlet El Veraz.

name: Antonio de la Cruz
outlet: Reporter for El Expresso
beat: Environmental issues were a more recent passion of De la Cruz, specifically drought and water shortages. Allegedly, while he did not work on security issues for Expresso, he frequently called out government officials on his personal social media accounts for corruption (examples here and here).
summary: Antonio de la Cruz was shot five times and killed by two armed men on a motorcycle at 9:10 a.m. as he walked to his car outside his home in Ciudad Victoria, Tamaulipas, to drive his daughter to school. She was shot in the head and died in hospital after emergency surgery failed. De la Cruz was a reporter known for his criticism of the Tamaulipas state government, and had reported no prior threats.

name: Ernesto Méndez
outlet: Editorial director of local newspaper Tu Voz; Contributor to Periódico Correo and Zona Franca
beat: General news
summary: Ernesto Méndez was shot dead with two other people at 11 p.m. in a bar and beer store he owned in Guanajuato; two more people were wounded. Earlier that day he had given a press conference in his capacity as a businessman, announcing that he had won a concession at the Northeast Regional Fair, and was said to be celebrating it. Local reports revealed that he had been receiving threats.

name: Allan González
outlet: Radio announcer at Switch 105.9 FM
beat: Music
summary: Allan González was killed with three colleagues from the radio station Switch 105.9 FM while they recorded a promotional segment from a mobile unit outside a pizzeria on Ejército Nacional Avenue in Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua; an armed group opened fire, killing them along with people inside the restaurant.

name: Armando Guerrero
outlet: Operations Manager at Switch 105.9 FM
beat: Non-editorial, operations manager
summary: Armando Guerrero, a non-editorial member of staff at the radio station Switch 105.9 FM, was killed alongside Allan González and two other colleagues while they recorded a promotional segment from a mobile unit outside a pizzeria on Ejército Nacional Avenue in Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua; an armed group opened fire, killing them along with people inside the restaurant.

name: Lino Flores
outlet: Promotional team at Switch 105.9 FM team
beat: Non-editorial, promo team
summary: Lino Flores, a non-editorial member of staff at the radio station Switch 105.9 FM, was killed alongside Allan González and two other colleagues while they recorded a promotional segment from a mobile unit outside a pizzeria on Ejército Nacional Avenue in Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua; an armed group opened fire, killing them along with people inside the restaurant.

name: Alejandro Arriaga
outlet: Security/bodyguard at Switch 105.9 FM team
beat: Non-editorial, bodyguard
summary: Alejandro Arriaga, a non-editorial member of staff at the radio station Switch 105.9 FM, was killed alongside Allan González and two other colleagues while they recorded a promotional segment from a mobile unit outside a pizzeria on Ejército Nacional Avenue in Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua; an armed group opened fire, killing them along with people inside the restaurant.

name: Juan Arjón López
outlet: Founder of A Qué le Temes
beat: Crime, local politics, and the environment. The most recent articles were posted on August 2 and included two short news stories about the arrests of suspects of robberies and theft.
summary: Juan Arjón López's body was found near an expressway in Sonora. He appeared to have died from a violent blow to the head.

name: Fredid Román
outlet: Founder and editor of La Realidad until it closed in 2022 due to financial difficulties from the COVID-19 pandemic. Then became a columnist for Vértice de Chilpancingo with his weekly “La Realidad Escrita” column; and columnist for La Realidad de Guerrero
beat: In his last post on social media almost an hour before being executed, titled "State Crime without Blaming the Boss," Román spoke about the Ayotzinapa case and criticized AMLO for "exonerating" his predecessor Enrique Peña Nieto of responsibility.
summary: Fredid Román was shot dead at about 4:30 p.m. by two men on a motorcycle as he got into his car outside his home in Chilpancingo, Guerrero. Román directed the news portal La Realidad and wrote columns for local Guerrero outlets, including the magazine Quehacer Político. The day before his murder, Román’s phone was targeted using telecommunications surveillance infrastructure in an attempt to extract location data and other information from his device, a technique consistent with SS7 network exploitation.

name: Pedro Pablo Kamul
summary: Pedro Pablo Kumul Amaya was shot dead while driving in the El Castillo area on the edge of Xalapa, Veracruz. He was pursued by another vehicle and his car crashed into a post, where he was found dead inside it. Kumul was a reporter and radio announcer for the Veracruz outlet AX Noticias and the station Es Amor 104.5 HD, and drove a taxi alongside that work.

name: Abisai Perez Romero
summary: Abisai Pérez Romero, an environmental journalist and student, was found dead in Tula, Hidalgo after disappearing one day before. At the time of his death, Pérez was investigating the socio-environmental impact of wastewater treatment facilities in the Mezquital Valley.

name: Jose Ramiro Araujo
outlet: News photographer
beat: General assignment photographer
summary: José Ramiro Araujo was stabbed by two youths who, according to reports, tried to steal his camera on the Bulevar Costero in Ensenada, Baja California. Araujo was a photojournalist and had been photographing a festival in the city for a local magazine when he was attacked.

name: Gerardo Torres Rentería
summary: Gerardo Torres Rentería was shot several times when armed men entered his home at about 9:30 p.m. in the Icacos neighbourhood of Acapulco, Guerrero,. Torres, 59, known as “El Negro Torres,” had been a correspondent for Reuters, TV Azteca and Telemundo and a cameraman for Televisa Acapulco, and founded the news portal Red Noticias.

name: Marco Aurelio Ramirez Hernandez
outlet: Freelance reporter
beat: Crime reporter for the news program "Cuarto Poder." Hosted a program on "Estéreo Luz FM" that analyzed various aspects of public life in the state of Puebla, including human rights violations and alleged irregularities in the exercise of public office.
summary: Marco Aurelio Ramírez Hernández was shot by armed men on a motorcycle while driving home in Tehuacán, Puebla. The court determined that the killing was directly related to the victim’s journalistic activity, specifically his investigation into criminal gangs operating in the Tehuacán region.

name: Luis Martín Sánchez Íñiguez
outlet: Correspondent for La Jornada; Contributor to criticadn.mx
beat: Three days before his disappearance, Sánchez Íñiguez published information released by the state prosecutor's office about eight bodies located and recovered from the clandestine grave known as 'devil's cave,' located on the lower northern slope of San Juan Hill, between the limits of Tepic and the municipality of Xalisco.
summary: Luis Martín Sánchez Íñiguez disappeared from his home in Tepic, Nayarit, on 5 July 2023 along with his laptop, phone and press card. His body was found three days later in the village of El Ahuacate, bound and showing signs of torture, with a message pinned to his chest with an ice pick reading “You can write whatever you want, but don’t mess with the family.” Sánchez was the Nayarit correspondent for the national newspaper La Jornada.

name: Nelson Matus Peña
outlet: Founder and editor for Lo Real de Guerrero
beat: Crime reporter. Lo Real de Guerrero often reported on instances of local violence. In the days before his death, Lo Real de Guerrero published several stories without a byline covering violent incidents and deadly shootouts in Acapulco.
summary: Nelson Matus Peña was shot twice, once in the head, just after 3 p.m. as he stood outside his car in the Emiliano Zapata neighbourhood of Acapulco, Guerrero. The head wound killed him. He had already survived one attempt on his life. He was the founder and director of the online news outlet Lo Real de Guerrero, a platform that focused extensively on coverage of violence and criminal activity in Acapulco.

name: Jesús Gutiérrez Vergara
outlet: Founder of Notiface Prensa Digital
beat: Known crime reporter. Gutiérrez had recently published an article about the arrest of an alleged drug trafficker and videos of police vehicles responding to an incident.
summary: Jesús Gutiérrez Vergara was talking with four off-duty police officers in a residential area of San Luis Río Colorado, Sonora when shots were fired from a vehicle, killing him and one of the officers and wounding the other three. His children were attacked by SEDENA soldiers in their home approximately one year after his murder.

name: Ismael Villagómez Tapia
outlet: Photojournalist for El Heraldo de Juárez
beat: General assignment photographer covering Juarez. Included coverage of the migrant caravan, and local crime. Last story was covering the casualties of a trailer crash in an area of ​​food stalls.
summary: Ismael Villagómez Tapia was shot at close range in his vehicle in Chihuahua. He is presumed to have been killed while working as a driver for the ride-hailing app InDrive after finishing his day at El Heraldo de Juárez, where he was a photographer. Two men accused of the killing were later acquitted.

name: Héctor Noguera Trujillo
summary: Héctor Noguera Trujillo, 76, was found dead in the bedroom of his home in the Zaragoza area of the port of Veracruz, with signs of violence, mainly blows to the head, and valuables missing from the house. State authorities treated the death as a killing during a robbery, though the governor said the first indication was natural causes. Noguera was a radio announcer for a local station, a writer, and a former director of the Veracruz City Museum.

name: Édgar Sifuentes Casso
summary: Édgar Sifuentes Casso, 33, disappeared on the night of 15 November 2023. His body was found the next morning on a dirt track in Valle Hermoso, Tamaulipas, with wounds from a sharp object. Sifuentes founder of the digital outlets La NETAM and Contenido Social and director of social communication for the Valle Hermoso municipality.

name: Mateo Gonzalez Jimenez
summary: Mateo González Jiménez, director of the radio station Maranatha, was shot dead alongside his wife inside their home in San Cristóbal de las Casas, Chiapas. Jiménez was the director of the Indigenous Christian radio station Radio Maranatha.

name: Roberto Carlos Figueroa
outlet: Founder and director of Acá En El Show
beat: Local politics. Figueroa often criticized Governor Cuauhtémoc Blanco Bravo with satirical and critical videos. Right before his murder, Figueroa posted a story about the murder of a brother of a candidate for the municipal elections in Tetecala, a city in the west of the state. On the day of his abduction and killing, Figueroa posted a short video on Acá en el Show announcing that he had information on corruption involving candidates for the upcoming June 2 state and federal elections.  The post appeared to be an announcement that he would release the information soon, though a date was not given.
summary: Roberto Carlos Figueroa was abducted by gunmen on the morning of 26 April 2024. in the morning after dropping his two daughters at school in Morelos. His unidentified captors contacted his wife multiple times, who paid a ransom. Figueroa’s body was discovered later that evening on a dirt road in Coajomulco, north of Cuernavaca. He had suffered a fatal gunshot wound to the head. Figueroa was the founder and editor of the digital news outlet Acá en el Show.

name: Martin Antonio Olivier Rodriguez
summary: Martín Antonio Olivier Rodríguez was found dead in a taxi in Ajalpan, Puebla, with gunshot wounds and signs of violence on 7 May 2024. He was reported missing by his relatives the day prior. Rodríguez was a broadcaster for La Que Más Suena 91.7 FM.

name: Víctor Alfonso Culebro Morales
outlet: Director of Realidades
beat: Local politics, cultural events, and security. One day before Morales' disappearance, Realidades published a report that the deployment of thousands of soldiers and police officers to Chiapas had failed to stem violence related to turf wars between criminal gangs.
summary: Víctor Alfonso Culebro Morales was reported missing on 27 June 2024. The next day, his body was found abandoned on the Ocozocoautla–Arriaga highway, near the Tierra y Libertad ejido in Chiapas. He was bound, his face taped, with bullet wounds and signs of torture. Culebro was the founder, director, and editor of Realidades, Periodismo con verdad

name: Alejandro Alfredo Martínez Noguéz
outlet: Director of El Hijo del Llanero Solititito
beat: Security and crime. His last publications included coverage of a murder, several citizen reports of vehicle thefts, and a disappearance.
summary: Alejandro Alfredo Martínez Noguez was shot dead on 4 August 2024, on the Villagrán–Celaya stretch of Federal Highway 45 in Guanajuato. Gunmen opened fire on the car in which he was travelling under police escort, wounding two of his bodyguards. He was enrolled in federal protection at the time of his murder. Martínez was a crime reporter who ran his own outlet, El Hijo del Llanero Solititito, after decades working for local radio stations and newspapers.

name: Enrique Hernández Avilés
summary: Enrique Hernández Avilés disappeared in Taxco de Alarcón, Guerrero, on 20 June 2024 after being stopped by traffic officers; his remains were found in a clandestine grave at Espejo Potrero, Taxco, at the start of September 2024 and identified by DNA. Hernández worked for the magazine Contacto Policiaco. Ten Taxco municipal police officers were detained over the case and four charged, three of them with aggravated kidnapping; press reports said he was taken to police premises, tortured and killed there.

name: Manuel Carmona Esquivel
summary: Manuel Carmona Esquivel was killed in Zitácuaro, Michoacán, alongside María Eufemia Reyes Esquivel and José Luis Chávez. A Purépecha man, he was a defender of Indigenous autonomy.

name: José Luis Chávez
summary: José Luis Chávez was killed in Zitácuaro, Michoacán, alongside Manuel Carmona Esquivel and María Eufemia Reyes Esquivel. A Purépecha man, he was a defender of Indigenous autonomy.
